increments.title: DR1 offers each species as its common name with the Latin name in brackets — 'African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)'; the frontend offers the bare Latin binomial, so a user who does not read Latin cannot tell the options apart.
increments.detail:
Every species option is labelled with its Latin binomial alone: under Cow (0102) the four choices read Bison bison, Bos spp., Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis; under Horse, Equus caballus; under Cat, Felis catus; under Dog, Canis lupus familiaris; under Fish, Salmo salar. There is no common name anywhere in the option set, because the catalogue does not hold one — each species is a value and a text and the text is the Latin name (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:15-26), rendered straight through as the checkbox label (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/view-model/commodity-groups.js:3-14). A user who knows the animal as a cow, a dog or a salmon never sees that word next to the box they have to tick.

DR1 labels a species with its common name first and the Latin name in brackets — 'African buffalo (Syncerus spp.)', 'Banteng (Novibos spp)', 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', 'Water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis)' — falling back to the commodity name in front of the Latin name when a species has no common name of its own (app/assets/javascripts/commodity-search.js:11-17). 123 of DR1's 144 species entries carry a commonName next to their label — every one of the 11 under Cattle (app/data/commodities-0102-species.js:3-15), the 3 under Horse and the 106 under Other live mammals, plus Cat, Dog and Ferret. The other 21, spread over the remaining 15 commodities, have none and take the fallback, so a user searching for sheep is offered 'Sheep (Ovis aries)' and one searching for ornamental fish is offered 'Ornamental fish (Cyprinidae)'. The common name is not decoration: it is what DR1's search matches on first, and the search hint tells the user so — 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).' The results panel is ordered by that display label rather than by the Latin name, which is why Cattle opens with African buffalo rather than Bison bison (app/utils/commodity-search-data.js:1-31).

Give every species in the catalogue a common name and render the option label as 'Common name (Latin name)', falling back to 'Commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name. This is presentation plus one extra piece of data per species, so it can be done in the frontend against the current stub before the real catalogue arrives — but it has to be in place before the search control ships, because DR1's search hint promises the user can find a commodity by its common name. increments.title: Frontend lets a user leave every "Number of animals" box empty and move on to the next page, and only refuses the notification later at the review gate; Design release 1 holds them on the page until each one is filled in.
increments.detail:
The count is checked for shape but never for presence. Each line gets one rule, an integer-in-range check with a minimum of one (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/fields.js:18-33), and that rule's schema explicitly allows the empty string, which short-circuits before the digits test runs (src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:123-143). So typing letters is refused — fe-consignment-details-error is that refusal — but pressing "Save and continue" with all four boxes blank is accepted and the user moves on to the next page. The frontend's own behaviour test records this: submitting a blank count re-renders no view and stores an empty string (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.test.js:150-168). The notification is not lost, only postponed: the count is a mandatory obligation (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:60-65), the stored empty string reads as unanswered (src/server/app/model/obligations/is-blank-value.js:6), so the commodities task never completes, the review section stays gated (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:83) and submission is refused (src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9-15). The user is stopped, just not at the point of the mistake and never with a reason.

Submitting the page with a count missing re-renders it with "Enter the number of animals" in the error summary, linked to that species' box, and repeats the message for every species left blank. Only once every count is present is the user moved on (app/routes.js:817-848).

Add a presence rule to the animal count on the consignment-details page, one per commodity line, with the message "Enter the number of animals", and add that message to the commodities copy file alongside the whole-number message already there (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:35-40) and to the Welsh file beside it. The page already renders an error summary and per-field errors, so this is a missing rule rather than a missing mechanism. The knock-on is the frontend's own count-drop check, which today reads a blank count as "no cap" when deciding whether identifier records would be orphaned; once a blank cannot be saved that branch has no live case and the check compares two real numbers. The feature's own test asserts that the blank saves, so it has to change with the rule. Nothing has to land first. Design release 1's consignment-details page was not photographed in its error state, so the observation that would confirm the anchor and the summary order is that page submitted with a count left blank.

increments.title: For commodity code 01061900 Design release 1 lists each chosen species as its own removable row in Selected commodities; Frontend gives the commodity one row and one Remove that drops every species under it.
increments.detail:
The Selected commodities table carries one row per commodity, whatever was chosen inside it. The captured page shows "01061900 / Dog / Remove" as a single row, and the table is built by collapsing the commodity lines to their distinct commodity names (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/view-model/groups.js:24-33, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/_selected-commodities-table.njk:4-19). Pressing Remove drops every line of that commodity at once (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/remove/post-remove.js:26-40). A user who has chosen two species under one 01061900 commodity has no way to drop one of them from this page — the only route back is to reopen the commodity page and untick it there. The catalogue behind the table is itself a hardcoded stub of five commodities and eight species with no reference-data client behind it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:1-26), so the two commodities it carries on code 01061900 — Cat and Dog — hold one species each.

Every commodity gets one row except those on commodity code 01061900, which get one row per chosen species, each named by that species' own common name and each carrying its own Remove (app/routes.js:626-645, against app/routes.js:672-682 for every other commodity). Removing one takes that species out and leaves the rest of the commodity in place. Design release 1's captured page shows cattle, which is not 01061900, so the picture shows the ordinary commodity-level row and this rule has to be read from where it is stated. The rule carries weight because of how deep that code goes on the requirements side: Design release 1 holds twenty-one live-animal commodities under their IPAFFS names and 144 species between them, four of them on 01061900 — Cat, Dog, Ferret and Other live mammals — and Other live mammals alone carries 106 species (app/data/commodities.js:9-290). A user who picks six of those sees six rows and six Removes on Design release 1 and one row and one Remove on Frontend.

On the consignment-details page, list each chosen species of a 01061900 commodity as its own row in Selected commodities, named by the species, with a Remove that takes out that species only and leaves the rest of the commodity. Everything else keeps the commodity-level row it has now. The frontend's stub already carries two commodities on that code — Cat and Dog (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:3-10) — and the difference already shows today even with one species each, because a per-species row is named by the species rather than by the commodity: on Design release 1 the dog row reads "Domestic dog", on Frontend it reads "Dog". A second species under either would then add a second row where Frontend still shows one. Removal already works line by line underneath: the store holds one line per species and only the page collapses them, so this is a change to the table and to what Remove submits rather than to the store.

The two runs band this work differently, and the band is the decision with money attached. Run C bands it frontend-work and says nothing has to land first, on the evidence just given: the store already holds one line per species, so the table and what Remove submits are the whole of the change and it can be built against today's stub. Run A saw the same difference and banded it needs-backend, because it read the per-species rows as one of three things that follow once the commodity and species catalogue comes from a reference-data API rather than a constants file — on that reading this waits for the API, for a client for it in the frontend, and for every lookup the frontend keys off a commodity name to move onto codes. The band carried here is run C's, because the judge found run C's evidence decisive on what is buildable today; run A would have banded it higher. Whoever rules on the band is choosing between a table-and-Remove change that can ship now and holding the selected-commodities table behind reference data.

FALSIFIED BY: Design release 1 rendering a single commodity-level row for a 01061900 commodity with two species chosen — for instance ferret and dog together. The selected-rows builder branches on the code before it branches on anything else, so a single row there would prove this wrong.

increments.title: Removing the last commodity leaves the Frontend user on an empty details page with a link to start again; Design release 1 takes them straight back to "What are you importing?".
increments.detail:
Remove always returns the user to the same page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/remove/post-remove.js:36-43). When the row removed was the last one, that page comes back empty: the selected-commodities table and the quantity blocks disappear, the heading and the buttons stay, and the body reads "You have not added any commodities yet." above a link now labelled "Add a commodity" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.njk:11-22, with the two labels chosen at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/consignment-details.controller.js:53-58). The user is on a page that asks nothing and has to notice the link.

Remove checks whether anything is left, and where nothing is it sends the user to the commodity question instead of re-rendering the page (app/routes.js:9377-9388). increments.title: Frontend labels the package count "Number of packages (optional)"; Design release 1 labels it "Number of packages (when required)".
increments.detail:
Each commodity line that asks for packages labels the field "Number of packages (optional)", with the hint "Such as crates, bags or boxes" beneath it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:32-35, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/_species-quantities.njk:24-34). "(optional)" is the GOV.UK convention for a field a user may always skip, so it tells the user the count never matters.

The same field, in the same position, is labelled "Number of packages (when required)" with the same hint (app/views/consignment-details.html:116-129, from the per-commodity field definition at app/data/commodities.js:21-23). "(when required)" says the opposite thing about the same box: that there are circumstances in which the count has to be given. The field is asked only for the commodities that can be packaged, and Design release 1 validates the count only on germinal lines, which a Design release 1 user cannot create (app/routes.js:900-932), so no live-animals user meets a package-count error on either side.

Change the package-count label from "Number of packages (optional)" to "Number of packages (when required)" in the commodities copy file, and the same in the Welsh file beside it. Note what the label change does not settle: neither side validates the box for live animals today, so the wording is the only place a user is told anything about when the count matters. If "when required" turns out to mean a rule rather than a hint, that rule is a separate change and Design release 1 does not state it. Nothing has to land first.

increments.title: On the commodity-details page Frontend sets the commodity heading, the species name and the quantity labels smaller and lighter than Design release 1, so the page loses the reading order the design gives it.
increments.detail:
Below the page heading the type steps down twice and then flattens. The commodity heading "Cow (0102)" is a medium heading, the species name "Bos taurus" below it is a small heading, and the two field labels — "Number of animals" and "Number of packages (optional)" — carry no size or weight at all, so they render in ordinary body text at the same size and weight as the hints under them (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/_species-quantities.njk:7, :9, :14 and :26). With four commodities on the captured page, the labels and the hints form an unbroken run of same-weight text and only the two headings break it up.

The commodity heading "Cattle (0102)" is 36px bold — the size of the page heading itself — the species name "Bos taurus" below it is 24px bold, and every field label on the page is 19px bold against a 19px light hint, so each question stands away from its own guidance (app/assets/sass/application.scss:1070-1112, the app-consignment-details-page block, whose .govuk-label rule at :1107-1112 sets weight 700). The captured page shows all three levels.

increments.title: The save and cancel controls at the foot of every journey page send the user back to "the hub"; Design release 1 calls the same page the overview
increments.detail:
Every journey page ends with the same three controls, built by one shared macro (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13): a primary "Save and continue" button, a secondary "Save and return to hub" button and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. The wording comes from src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45. Both strings appear on 41 of the 67 captured frontend screens. The page they name is headed "Overview", so the word "hub" appears nowhere the user can see it except on these two controls — it is the internal name for the task list.

Design release 1 uses the same three-control pattern with the same primary label, and names the destination after what it is headed: "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" (app/views/consignment-details.html:145). Both strings appear on 29 of the 60 captured screens. The design's own task-list page is headed "Overview" as well, so on that side the button and the page it leads to say the same word.

Rename saveAndReturnToHub to "Save and return to overview" and cancelAndReturnToHub to "Cancel and return to overview" in src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45. Both keys are read only by src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13, so one edit changes every page. The three controls and their order do not move, and the key names themselves can stay as they are; only the strings are user-visible. The Welsh pair in copy.cy.js is translated to match, and any frontend spec that locates these two controls by their text needs updating in the same change. The primary button beside them, however, does not always agree, and this rename does not touch it: on seven captured frontend screens the primary reads "Continue" where the Design release 1 screen it pairs with reads "Save and continue" — the three consignment-addresses hub states (fe-addresses-hub, -empty and -complete, against dr1-roles-and-addresses and dr1-roles-and-addresses-answered) and the four documents states (fe-documents, -populated, -scanning and -error, against the dr1-upload-documents family). It is not a blanket difference: on check-your-answers and on the declaration both sides read "Continue", so the two designs agree there. That primary label does not come from src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45 and is not read by src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 — each of those pages passes its own — so it is a different edit in different files and it is recorded here as an observation rather than folded into this rename.

increments.title: Frontend reads a saved animal back as one run-together line labelled "Animal 1"; Design release 1 reads it back in a table with a column per identifier and the species in the row label
increments.detail:
Once an animal is saved it becomes one row of a summary list above the entry form: a key reading "Animal 1" and a value reading "Ear tag: UK123456789012" — every filled identifier joined into a single sentence with its own label repeated inside it, so two identifiers read "Passport: UK123456789, Ear tag: UK123456789012", or the words "No identifier provided" if none were filled (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/identifier/summary.js:9-18, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:12-24). There is no header row, so nothing tells a trader which identifiers this commodity expects; a cattle animal saved on an ear tag alone and one saved on both reads as two lines of different lengths and nothing marks which is which, and a reader comparing two animals has to find the identifier name inside each sentence rather than reading down a column. The row is labelled by position rather than by animal — "Animal 1" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:87) — so on a page holding four commodity lines the same three words head the first row of every one of them.

Design release 1 reads the same information back as a table underneath the entry form: a header row of "Animal" and then one column per identifier the commodity declares — for cattle, "Ear tag" and "Passport" — then a row per saved animal whose key is the species and its number, "Bos taurus 1", with each identifier in its own cell and a Remove at the end (app/views/partials/animal-identification-saved-animals.html:1-28). Because the columns come from the commodity's own identifier list, a trader can see at a glance which identifiers are expected and which cells are still empty, and the row label says which animal of which species it is. One thing the table does not show is a partly filled animal: Design release 1's saved list carries only records whose every identifier holds a value, where Frontend lists every appended record including ones reading "No identifier provided".

Replace the summary list of saved animals with a table: a header row naming each identifier the commodity declares, one row per saved animal keyed by species and number, one cell per identifier, and the existing Remove in the last cell. The identifier labels are already in the copy file the header row needs (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:48-55) and the card view model already knows which identifiers apply to the line, so this is a template and view-model change with no new data. Frontend already renders this exact shape elsewhere in the journey, on the check-answers page at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/cards/consignment/species/identifier-table.js:9-24, which is the nearest thing to a working model of the target. Land it after identification--identifier-labels, which fixes the labels the header row would use, and note that whichever way identification--identifier-completeness is settled changes what an empty cell means rather than whether the table is right.

increments.title: A trader cannot record a microchip number for a horse, cat, dog or ferret anywhere in Frontend; Design release 1 asks for one on all of them
increments.detail:
Frontend knows six ways to identify an animal and a microchip is not one of them: passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name, and — only for commodities that have no specific identifier at all — free-text identification details and a description (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198). Which of the four specific types appear is decided by four commodity allowlists in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-115. The word microchip appears nowhere in src/server outside a test fixture, where it is typed as a value into the free-text field. The gap bites hardest on the commodities that need it: because dogs and horses do have specific identifiers, the free-text fallback is switched off for them, so a trader importing a dog is shown a passport and a tattoo field and nothing else. The captured DOM of fe-animal-identification bears this out — the dog line offers animalIdentifierPassport-2 and animalIdentifierTattoo-2, the horse line animalIdentifierPassport-1 and horseName-1, and there is nowhere on the page to put a chip number.

Design release 1 asks for a microchip on both identifier sets a companion animal or an equine falls into. Its identifiers are declared per commodity code, and a horse (0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name while a cat, dog, ferret or other live mammal — all of them commodity code 01061900 — is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo (app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19). Microchip is the first field on both panels, so it is the identifier the design puts in front of the trader first. Microchipping is how a dog is identified in law, so the field is not decoration.

Add a microchip identifier and apply it to the equine and companion-animal commodities — horse, cat, dog and ferret, not the dog and horse alone. In Frontend that is a seventh obligation beside passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, a MICROCHIP_COMMODITIES allowlist beside the existing four in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-115 written in the stub's picker-name vocabulary, a label and an error message in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72, the new obligation id added to the unit record's requires.anyOfIds so a microchip on its own satisfies the at-least-one-identifier rule, and its addition to the specific-identifier union so the free-text fallback keeps behaving as it does today. It cannot stop there: the value has to reach the outbox, and the animal identifier record the backend sends to GBNAG recognises only the type codes EAR_TAG and PASSPORT (trade-imports-animals-backend, TradeProductInstance.AnimalIdentifier), so a MICROCHIP type code and the field that feeds it are backend work that has to land alongside. The two runs of this comparison banded the work differently and it is worth being explicit about: run A read it as frontend-work and scoped the change to frontend files alone, run C banded it needs-backend on the strength of that contract. It is banded needs-backend here, and what turns on the answer is whether the change can be planned as a frontend-only ticket — it cannot, because a microchip captured in the frontend would have nowhere to go once the notification is sent.

FALSIFIED BY: A microchip field rendered on Frontend's animal identification page for a horse, cat, dog or ferret, or a microchip value carried anywhere in Frontend's notification payload. This was read from source on both sides and not photographed: Design release 1's identification capture was taken with cattle selected, whose identifiers are ear tag and passport, so no capture in this corpus shows the field. Capturing dr1-animal-identification-details with commodity 01061900 or 0101 selected would show it.

increments.title: Frontend makes a trader type the animals' permanent address in full; Design release 1 lets them reuse the place of destination address instead
increments.detail:
On the animal identification page, any animal whose commodity requires a permanent address gets a bare "Permanent address" heading followed by nine empty fields, all of them visible at once. There is no choice to make and nothing to reuse: the trader retypes the name, address, postcode, country, telephone and email for every such animal, even when the animals are going to live at the place of destination they have already given elsewhere in the notification. The block is rendered whenever the commodity requires an address, with nothing gating the fields inside it, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43-69, and the nine fields it loops over are fixed at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/address/fields.js:126-163.

Design release 1 asks "Where will their permanent address be?" and offers each animal a two-option radio, "Select an address": "Same as the place of destination (POD)", or "Enter a new address", which opens the address fields as a conditional reveal and is hinted "This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination." Picking the first answers the question in one click, and once a place of destination has been given it is printed as a hint under that option so the trader can see the address they are agreeing to. The two options are built at app/routes.js:2479-2500.

Add a two-option radio above the permanent address fields on the animal identification card — reuse the place of destination address, or enter a new one — and hide the address fields behind the second option. The frontend already collects a place of destination as one of its five consignment parties (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:51-55), so the address to copy is in the notification already and nothing outside the frontend has to change. Show the chosen destination address as the hint on the first option, as Design release 1 does, so the trader is not agreeing to an address they cannot see. Run A prescribes the same choice in a different place — on the new permanent-address page it asks for, rather than inside the existing identification card — so read this together with inc-057, which moves the question onto that page. Adding the radio to the card is the smaller, standalone change; once the page exists the choice belongs on it.

FALSIFIED BY: A radio, checkbox or "same as" link anywhere in the frontend's permanent address block that copies an address the trader has already given. The captured DOM of fe-animal-identification contains no input of type radio or checkbox at all.

increments.title: Frontend asks which country the animals will permanently live in; Design release 1 does not ask for a country on the permanent address
increments.detail:
The permanent address block ends with a mandatory "Country" select offering thirty-two countries — the United Kingdom, the EU member states and the rest of the EEA plus Switzerland — under the placeholder "Select a country". Leaving it blank once any other address field has been filled produces "Select a country", and choosing a value outside the list produces "Select a country from the list" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/address/fields.js:66-70, 147-153). So the frontend treats the place an imported animal will live as a question with thirty-two possible answers.

Design release 1 asks for eight fields and no country: name or organisation name, address line 1, address line 2 (optional), town or city, county (optional), postcode or zip code, email address and phone number (app/views/partials/permanent-address-new-address-fields.html:6-97, revealed under "Enter a new address" and rendered in dr1-permanent-address-animals-new-address-revealed). It does not need one, because the page has already said what this address is for: somewhere the animal "will permanently reside" and "can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)". An address APHA can inspect is a Great Britain address, so there is nothing to choose.

Remove the Country select and its two validation messages from the animal permanent address block, leaving the eight fields Design release 1 asks for. Nothing else in the journey reads the value: it is collected, checked against the country list and written into the animal's address record, and no other page or rule depends on it. This is the one field on this block where the frontend asks the trader for more than the signed-off design does, so removing it shortens the form rather than lengthening it.

increments.title: Frontend counts an animal as identified once one identifier is filled in; Design release 1 does not count it until every identifier for that commodity is filled in
increments.detail:
One identifier is enough. A trader who fills the ear tag and leaves the passport blank presses "Save and add another", the animal is added to the summary list as "Animal 1 — Ear tag: UK123456789012", and the counter moves on to "Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2". Only an entirely empty animal is refused, with "Enter at least one identifier for this animal" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:140), which is the rule the obligation states as a requires-any-of over the six identifier fields (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:89-98). fe-animal-identification-saved and fe-animal-identification-at-maximum both show animals saved on an ear tag alone.

Design release 1 appears to require all of them. An animal counts as entered only when every identifier declared for its commodity carries a value (app/routes.js:1526-1532), so a cattle animal needs both an ear tag and a passport and a horse needs a microchip, a passport and a horse name. A partly filled animal is not refused and no error is shown — the page simply re-renders the same animal with the values kept and the counter unmoved, and the saved-animals table lists only complete animals. That is a silent outcome rather than a stated rule, which is what makes this finding uncertain.

This is disputed because the two sources of the requirement disagree, and the two readings imply opposite work: if all identifiers are required, Frontend has to change the unit record's requires from an any-of over the six identifier ids to a rule over the identifier obligations in scope for that commodity line, move the individual identifier obligations from optional to mandatory so each empty box names itself in the error summary rather than the record failing as a whole, and write the error copy for it, which Design release 1 does not supply because it shows no message at all; if they are not required, Frontend is already right and this finding should be struck. Any such change also has to follow the commodity identifier sets being corrected, because the rule is only as good as the set it ranges over — with tattoo still on cattle it would demand a tattoo for every cow. Design release 1's behaviour is not in doubt — its entry form holds a trader on an animal until every identifier for that commodity carries a value, and its saved list only ever shows complete animals. What is in doubt is whether that behaviour states a requirement, because the data-fields specification Frontend implements says the opposite in words: the obligation carries the V4 line "Field Block - Mandatory to Submit - At least one Animal Identifier" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:66-72). The two runs of this comparison read that differently and banded it differently — run A took Design release 1's behaviour at face value, banded the work frontend-work and prescribed the requires-all change outright, where run C found the V4 contradiction and banded it disputed. It is banded disputed here, and what turns on the answer is whether there is any work at all: on run A's reading the change above is scheduled, on run C's the frontend is already correct. The one observation that would settle it is a statement from the design authority on which of the two governs — Design release 1's silent per-field behaviour, or the V4 field block. No capture can settle it; see the correction for why the capture originally proposed here cannot fire.

FALSIFIED BY: An error message in Design release 1 naming a missing identifier, or a line in the V4 data-fields specification requiring every identifier for a commodity rather than at least one. Design release 1's identifier validator returns an empty error list unconditionally (app/routes.js:1776-1786), so the design has no way to tell a trader that an identifier is missing.

increments.title: A trader who has miscounted the animals has no way out of Frontend's identification page; Design release 1 offers a Change number of animals link on every species panel
increments.detail:
Each card is headed with the commodity and species and then a counter — "Enter details for Bos taurus 1 of 2" — and that counter is the only thing on the card that mentions the number the trader is being held to. increments.title: Frontend buries the animals' permanent address inside the identification form; Design release 1 asks for it as its own step in the consignment parties section
increments.detail:
The frontend has no permanent address page. For a commodity that needs one, the nine address fields are printed inside the animal identification card, between the identifier fields and the "Save and add another" button, under a small heading (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:43-69). A trader meets the question only while entering identifiers for that animal, and the only route back to it is to reopen animal identification. On the captured page it appears once, on the dog line, and a trader scrolling for it has to know it is there. It is asked for cats and dogs alone, because those are the only commodities in the frontend's catalogue that require an address (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:115).

Design release 1 gives the question a page of its own, captioned "Consignment parties" and headed "Permanent address", reached from the parties list and back-linked to it (app/routes.js:2770-2777). It is a member of the consignment address sections for commodity code 01061900 alongside place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:124-131), so it is one step among the addresses a notification carries, answered once for every animal on that line and revisitable like any other. That commodity code is the whole 01061900 group — cat, dog, ferret and other live mammals — not cats and dogs alone. It is also one page rather than two: /permanent-address writes no to the same-as-destination answer and redirects straight to the select page (app/routes.js:10789-10801), and the sibling view asking whether all the animals are going to the place of destination is dead code, its renderer at app/routes.js:2780 having no callers.

Move the permanent address out of the identification card and give it its own page in the addresses section, listing every animal that needs one, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back. The frontend already renders five party pages from one template driven by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js, which is the shape this page takes; the obligation is already per-animal (permanentAddress sits within the unit record at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:200-208), so no model change is needed. Land this before the same-as-destination choice and the guidance copy, because both of those belong on the page this creates. The applicability difference rides with the commodity catalogue rather than with this page: Design release 1 asks the question for the whole 01061900 group where the frontend asks it only for cats and dogs, and that cannot be reproduced until the catalogue grows past its five entries.

increments.title: Frontend gives one sentence about the animals' permanent address; Design release 1 warns that a false address is fraud and explains what a permanent address is

increments.title: Frontend heads its two identification pages "Animal identification details" and "Additional animal details"; Design release 1 names them "Identification details" and "Additional details"
increments.detail:
Both pages in this section put the word "animal" in their own name. The identifier page is headed "Animal identification details" and the extra-facts page "Additional animal details" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:43 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/additional-details/copy/copy.en.js:2). Each name is used three times on its page — as the h1, as the last breadcrumb and as the browser tab title — so a trader reads it repeatedly. Design release 1 names the same two pages "Identification details" and "Additional details", and puts the section above them instead: "About the consignment" over the first (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:3, with the caption and heading at :44-47) and "Commodity details" over the second (app/views/additional-animal-details.html:9, caption and heading at :37-38). Rename the two pages to "Identification details" and "Additional details", in English and Welsh. Each name lives once, in its feature's copy file, and feeds the heading, the breadcrumb and the tab title together. This is one string per page and nothing has to land first. It covers the pages' own names only: what the hub calls these two tasks is raised separately as hub--task-row-labels, which asks for the same two words on the task rows. It reads best alongside the section caption, which the service-wide slice owns and which is what makes the shorter names self-explanatory — without a caption above it "Additional details" is a heading that says less than the one it replaces — but it does not depend on it, and the shorter names are the signed-off ones either way.

increments.title: Frontend labels the animal identifier fields "Passport number" and "Ear tag number"; Design release 1 labels them "Passport" and "Ear tag"
increments.detail:
Two of the identifier fields carry a longer label than the signed-off design uses: "Passport number" and "Ear tag number" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72). Frontend's own summary of a saved animal already uses the short forms — the label list it renders identifiers under is "Passport", "Tattoo", "Ear tag" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:48-55) — so a trader is shown one name while entering a value and a different name after saving it. "Tattoo" and "Horse name" match the design as they are. Each field also carries a worked example as a hint, "For example, UK123456789" and "For example, UK123456789012", which Design release 1 states nowhere.

Design release 1 labels its identifiers with the bare name of the thing: Ear tag, Passport, Tattoo, Microchip, Horse name. The labels are declared once per commodity code and used both on the entry form and as the column headings of the saved-animals table (app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-31), which is why the label a trader types under and the label they read back are the same word.

Change the two labels to "Passport" and "Ear tag" in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:58-72, with the Welsh siblings to match. increments.title: Design release 1 asks the purpose and exit questions as conditional reveals under the import reason the user has just chosen; Frontend hides them until the next page and asks each one on a page of its own.
increments.detail:
Choosing an import reason reveals nothing. The captured screenshot of fe-import-reason-transit-selected shows Transit selected and the next thing on the page is the Save and continue button — no port of exit, no destination country. The follow-up questions are separate pages reached only after the user submits, in the fixed order purpose, destination country, port of exit, exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:49-57), and the hub carries them as a second, conditional task row of their own (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:34-39). So Internal market costs a user two page loads, Transhipment or onward travel two, Transit three and Temporary admission horses three, where Design release 1 costs one. A user answering for transit therefore visits three pages and crosses two hub tasks to answer one question and its consequences. Two further differences travel with the split and disappear with it. First, each of the split-out pages says its own name three times — breadcrumb, page heading and field label — so fe-destination-country reads "Destination country / Destination country / Destination country" down the left of the page, from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/template.njk:8 and :16; fe-port-of-exit and fe-exit-date are the same shape. Second, each carries hint text that Design release 1's reveal does not: "The country the consignment travels on to after Great Britain." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/copy/copy.en.js:5) and the leading sentence of "The date the animals are expected to leave Great Britain. For example, 27/3/2026" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:5) — text a field only needs once it has been stranded on a page with no surrounding question. Both reasons that ask two questions ask them in the opposite order to Design release 1's: Transit asks destination country and then port of exit, and Temporary admission horses asks port of exit and then exit date, because the four pages sit in one fixed sequence and every reason walks the same sequence.

The reason page answers itself. Each importReason radio that has follow-up questions opens them inline underneath it as a conditional reveal, so the user reads the reason, chooses it, answers what it needs and presses Save and continue once (app/views/reason-for-import.html:47-62). Internal market opens the "Purpose in the internal market" question with its eleven radios; Transhipment or onward travel opens a Destination country select; Transit opens Port of exit and then Destination country; Temporary admission horses opens Exit date and then Port of exit; Re-entry opens nothing. No reveal carries a page heading, and only two of them carry any text beyond a field label: the internal-market reveal heads its radios with a medium fieldset legend reading "Purpose in the internal market", and the exit date carries the worked example "For example, 27/3/2026". The other three fields are a bare label over a select, because the radio's own hint above them already supplies the context. Every reveal is present in the rendered page and hidden until its radio is chosen, which is why a captured temporary-admission state carries all six reveal fields in its DOM (app/routes.js:8778-8820). Six rather than four because Design release 1 gives each branch its own field name: it renders two destination-country selects and two port-of-exit selects on the one page, with identical labels, identical 41-entry and 10-entry lists and identical error text, and the review page collapses each pair back to a single row keyed on the reason. Two inputs cannot share a name attribute, so the per-branch prefixes are a DOM artefact rather than a sixth and seventh question, and nothing here asks Frontend to hold two of either field.

Move the four questions onto the reason page as conditional reveals under the radio that requires them, and delete the four pages, the conditional exit-details task row and the four page-name headings that go with them. Nothing has to land first: the two sides already agree exactly on when each question applies, so no obligation changes. src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js gates purposeInInternalMarket on internalMarket (:43-56), destinationCountry on transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel (:66-79), portOfExit on transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses (:86-99) and exitDate on temporaryAdmissionHorses (:103-116), and Design release 1 reveals exactly the same four sets. Take each reveal's internal order from Design release 1 — port of exit then destination country under Transit, and exit date then port of exit under Temporary admission horses. Once the questions sit under their radio, drop the destination-country hint and the leading sentence of the exit-date hint, keeping the worked example "For example, 27/3/2026" that Design release 1 also shows; that copy work is booked on its own as inc-068, and the Exit details hub row this change retires is booked as inc-069, so the three can be scheduled together or the reveal move taken on its own. What happens to an answer when the reason changes needs no decision of its own: both sides purge a reveal answer once its reason is no longer chosen — every Design release 1 POST to the reason page writes null to each branch field belonging to a reason other than the one submitted, and Frontend's obligation gates take the same four fields out of scope and purge them — so nothing about a flip moves either. If anything Frontend keeps more than Design release 1 does, because its single destinationCountry field serves both Transit and Transhipment, so a country answered under Transit is still in scope under Transhipment where Design release 1's transhipment field starts empty; that is the same per-branch-naming artefact and not a requirement.

FALSIFIED BY: A conditional reveal opening under any importReason radio on the frontend. The captured DOM of fe-import-reason has no govuk-radios__conditional element at all and no aria-controls on any of the five radios; finding one would prove this wrong.

increments.title: The frontend explains the destination country, the port of exit and the exit date with guidance DR1 does not have; DR1 asks all three with a bare label, and one of the frontend's sentences will be untrue once the exit port list is corrected.
increments.detail:

Port of exit reads 'Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list.' Exit date reads 'The date the animals are expected to leave Great Britain. For example, 27/3/2026' — the example, plus a sentence of explanation in front of it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/copy/copy.en.js:5, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:5). All three are text a field only needs once it has been stranded on a page with no surrounding question: the explanation the reason radio would otherwise be carrying, restated under a field that now has a page to itself.

increments.title: A user importing from the Canary Islands, Jersey or French Guiana cannot say so: the frontend's country list holds only sovereign states, where DR1 offers fourteen regions and territories alongside them.
increments.detail:
Both the country of origin and the destination country are drawn from one list of 31 entries, all of them sovereign states, and the same list serves both pages (src/server/app/services/countries/index.js:24, and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/destination-country/controller.js:27 reads it for the destination question). It holds four countries DR1 does not offer — Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland — and no regions or territories at all. Three entries are also named differently: Czechia, Ireland and 'Netherlands (the)'.

DR1 offers 41 entries on both questions: the 27 member states plus fourteen regions and dependencies, each labelled with its parent in brackets — Azores (Portugal), Canary Islands (Spain), Ceuta (Spain), French Guiana (France), Guadeloupe (France), Guernsey (United Kingdom), Isle of Man (United Kingdom), Jersey (United Kingdom), Madeira (Portugal), Martinique (France), Mayotte (France), Melilla (Spain), Reunion (France) and Saint Martin (France). It names the three contested entries Czech Republic, Republic of Ireland and Netherlands. It offers no EFTA states. The list is release-agnostic data in app/data/countries.js:1-79 and it also feeds the region-of-origin prefix table, so an entry missing from it has no prefix either.

Replace the country list with DR1's 41 entries and its labels, on both the origin and destination questions. It is one list change in the countries service and both pages pick it up. Settle whether dropping Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland is intended before removing them — DR1 not offering them may be an omission rather than a rule, and the frontend's list comes from a reference data service rather than a file, so the change may be a query rather than an edit.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that DR1's country select is populated from a design-release-specific list, so that the fourteen regions are visible only to a DR2 session and a DR1 user sees the same 31 states the frontend offers.

The fourteen named in the prototype slot match app/data/countries.js exactly. Stop blocking on country of origin at the page and let a partly answered origin page save. Keep the field mandatory for completeness, so the hub still shows the task as unfinished and the review page still stops a submission without it. The same save-what-you-have behaviour already applies on the frontend's reason-for-import page, so the pattern exists — this brings origin into line with it. increments.title: The frontend rejects an internal reference containing a space, hyphen or slash; DR1 accepts whatever the user's own system calls the consignment.
increments.detail:
The field invites 'any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment', but only letters, numbers and underscores get through. Typing ACME-2026/01, or a reference with a space in it, returns the page with 'Internal reference must only contain letters, numbers and underscores'. There is also a 58-character ceiling, with 'Internal reference must be 58 characters or less' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/origin/controller.js:75-82).

DR1 asks the same optional question with the same label and the same hint, and imposes no rule on it at all: the submitted value is trimmed and stored, and no length or character check runs (app/routes.js:9240-9244). A user pastes in whatever reference their own records use.

Drop the character rule so hyphens, slashes, spaces and full stops are accepted — the whole point of the field is that it is the user's own reference and the service does not read it. Keep a length ceiling if downstream storage needs one, but say the limit in the hint rather than only in an error, and confirm 58 is a real constraint rather than an arbitrary one, because DR1 states no limit.

FALSIFIED BY: Submitting DR1's origin page with an internal reference containing a hyphen and being returned to the page with an error about the characters used.

increments.title: Frontend heads the reason page with the question "What is the main reason for importing the animals?" and names it "Reason for import"; Design release 1 heads it "Main reason for import" and keeps the question as a hidden legend.
increments.detail:

At the captured width the question wraps onto two lines, pushing the first radio down the screen before the user has read a single option. increments.title: Frontend lets a user leave the internal-market purpose blank and carry on; Design release 1 keeps them on the page with "Select a purpose in the internal market" until it is answered.
increments.detail:
A user who chooses Internal market, reaches the purpose page with its eleven radios, selects nothing and presses Save and continue is taken to the next page. The page has no error message to show and its copy file carries none for a blank answer — it validates with oneOf, which treats an empty string as a valid choice (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/controller.js:25-30, and the validator itself at src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:114-121). Frontend is not permissive everywhere on this journey: destination country and port of exit both use requiredOneOf and both produce an error, which the captured screens fe-destination-country-error and fe-port-of-exit-error show. The notification is not submittable in this state — purposeInInternalMarket is mandatory once in scope (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:43-56), and the review section is gated on every task row being fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15, applied at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85, the gate itself at :83). So this is not a hole a user can submit through: it is a user who is let past the question and told nothing, meets a hub row they cannot clear, and finds out only when the check-answers step will not open.

Choosing Internal market and leaving the revealed purpose blank returns the user to the same page with an error summary and an error against the field. Design release 1 says which message goes with the gap: "Select a purpose in the internal market" (app/routes.js:1387-1441, and the check itself at :1387-1394). Save and continue returns the page with "There is a problem" and one entry, the same message appears in red inside the reveal above the eleven radios, the reveal is left open with the red bar running down its edge, and the summary link moves focus to the first radio. Design release 1 carries the rule at the later points too — the hub reads the reason task as complete only when the purpose is present (app/routes.js:1343-1367), and Continue on the review page is refused without it (app/routes.js:10068-10075) — so the difference is where the rule bites, not whether it exists. The main reason itself is deliberately not enforced: the design states in its own words that "a main reason is optional to proceed, but once selected any further information required for that reason must be completed" (app/routes.js:1381-1385), so the two sides already agree about the reason radio and disagree only about what hangs off it.

Make purposeInInternalMarket required at the point it is asked, so a blank answer returns the page with an error summary rather than advancing: swap oneOf for requiredOneOf and add the message "Select a purpose in the internal market" to src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/copy/copy.en.js, which today has no errors block at all. Do not make the reason radio required — Design release 1 lets a user leave it blank and Frontend already matches that. Nothing has to land first; the obligation model already marks the field mandatory, so this only moves the moment the user is told. If inc-067 lands first and the purpose becomes a conditional reveal on the reason page, the same check belongs on the reveal instead of on a page that will no longer exist, shown as Design release 1 shows it.

increments.title: Frontend lets a user leave the exit date blank on a temporary-admission-horses import and carry on; Design release 1 keeps them on the page with "Enter an exit date", a message that exists nowhere in the service.
increments.detail:
Exit date is a date picker on a page of its own, reached only when the reason is Temporary admission horses. Leave the box empty, press Save and continue, and the journey moves on: the page validates with dateText, which allows an empty string through before it ever tries to read a date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/controller.js:21 and src/server/app/lib/validate/validators.js:209-234). The only message the page owns is "Enter a real exit date" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/exit-date/copy/copy.en.js:8), and there is no message for the date being missing anywhere in the service — the string "Enter an exit date" appears nowhere in trade-imports-animals-frontend or trade-imports-animals-tests. The rule itself is not missing: exitDate is mandatory once in scope (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:103-116), so the Exit details hub row stays incomplete, and the review section is gated on every task row being fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15, applied at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85, the gate itself at :83). So this is not a hole a user can submit through: it is a user who is let past the question and told nothing, and who finds out only when the check-answers step will not open.

Choosing Temporary admission horses and leaving the exit date blank returns the user to the same page with an error summary and an error against the field, and Design release 1 distinguishes the two failures: an empty box gives "Enter an exit date" and one it cannot read gives "Enter a real date" (app/routes.js:1424-1432, within the block that holds all five reason-page messages at :1387-1441). The same submit also requires the port of exit, so a user leaving both blank sees two entries in the summary. Design release 1 carries the rule at the later points too — the hub reads the reason task as complete only when both are present (app/routes.js:1343-1367), and Continue on the review page is refused without them (app/routes.js:10068-10075) — so the difference is where the rule bites, not whether it exists. The main reason itself is deliberately not enforced: the design states in its own words that "a main reason is optional to proceed, but once selected any further information required for that reason must be completed" (app/routes.js:1381-1385), so the two sides already agree about the reason radio and disagree only about what hangs off it.

Make exitDate required at the point it is asked, so a blank answer returns the page with an error summary rather than advancing: add a required check ahead of the date parse with the message "Enter an exit date". Do not make the reason radio required — Design release 1 lets a user leave it blank and Frontend already matches that. Nothing has to land first; the obligation model already marks the field mandatory, so this only moves the moment the user is told. Align the invalid-date message in the same pass if it has not already been done: Design release 1 says "Enter a real date" where Frontend says "Enter a real exit date", and that string is booked with the rest of the exit-message copy as inc-075. If inc-067 lands first and the exit date becomes a conditional reveal on the reason page, the same check belongs on the reveal instead of on a page that will no longer exist. The extra sentence Frontend puts in front of the exit-date hint is a separate copy change, booked as inc-068.

increments.title: Four of the eleven internal-market purpose hints read differently on Frontend than in Design release 1, including "it's" where it should be "its" and "e.g." where Design release 1 writes "for example".
increments.detail:
The eleven purpose options and their order match Design release 1 exactly, but four of the hints beneath them do not. Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift reads "Any movement of an animal that has as it's aim, the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the animal ... with no sale involved (e.g. a gift)" — a wrong possessive, a comma splitting "aim" from what follows, "e.g." instead of words, and no closing full stop. Three more end without a full stop: Breeding, "... or produce offspring"; Racing, competition, show or training, "Animals to participate in competitive or training events"; and Production, "... any other animal product or by-product". All four come from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/import-purpose/copy/copy.en.js:6, :10, :13 and :19. The other seven hints — Rescue, Research, Approved premises or body, Companion animal not for resale or rehoming, Slaughter, Fattening and Restocking — match word for word.

Design release 1 writes the same four hints in plain, correct English and closes every one of them with a full stop: "Any movement of an animal that has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the animal ... with no sale involved (for example a gift).", "... or produce offspring.", "Animals to participate in competitive or training events." and "... any other animal product or by-product." (app/data/internal-market-purposes.js:7, :17, :27, :42). The eleven purposes and their hints live in release-agnostic data, so this is what a Design release 1 user reads.

Replace those four hint strings in the frontend's import-purpose copy with Design release 1's wording: fix "it's" to "its", drop the comma after "aim", spell "e.g." out as "for example" as GDS style requires, and add the missing full stop to all four. One file, four strings, no behaviour change and nothing has to land first. The eleven options, their order and their labels already match, so nothing else on the page moves. Do the Welsh file in the same pass if the same drift is in it. One guard rail: the awkward "traveling" spelling in the Companion animal hint is shared by both sides, so it is not part of this change and must not be tidied along the way.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding "its aim" or a closing full stop on the sale/gift hint in fe-import-purpose's captured DOM. It renders "has as it's aim, the sale of" and ends "(e.g. a gift)" with no stop.

increments.title: Frontend lets a user pick any port of entry as the port of exit; Design release 1 offers only the border control posts approved for animals leaving Great Britain.
increments.detail:
The port-of-exit select is the port-of-entry list. Its captured DOM offers 80 options — a "Select port of exit" placeholder, a disabled separator and 78 ports — running from "Aberdeen Airport (GB DYC)" to the far end of the alphabet, each labelled with a UN location code, and including inland and cargo terminals such as "Nottingham Port (GB NTG)" and "HES Humber Bulk Terminal (GB HMR)". Nothing marks which of the 78 can handle animals and any of them is accepted, so a user can choose a port their consignment cannot lawfully leave from. The page says so out loud: the field's hint reads "Choose where the consignment will leave Great Britain. Exit and entry share the same port list." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/copy/copy.en.js:5). This is a design decision rather than fixture contents. The controller builds the options by mapping the single shared ports service (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/port-of-exit/controller.js:22-29) and validates the answer against that same list (:32-38); the service holds one list and primes it from the reference-data service's ports-of-entry endpoint (src/server/app/services/ports/client.js:4-6), and every record it returns is exactly a code and a name, with no designation to filter on (src/server/app/services/ports/index.js:9-14). There is no exit list and no filter over the entry list. The frontend's own obligation records where the decision came from: "Port selected from the port of entry list (Exit and Entry share the same list)" at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:81-83.

The port of exit is a short, purpose-built list of ten border control posts approved to handle animals: Edinburgh, Gatwick, Glasgow, three Heathrow posts, Holyhead, Manchester, Prestwick and Stansted, each carrying its BCP code. Design release 1 keeps it in its own file, separate from the arrival ports, and names it for what it is (app/data/exit-border-control-posts.js:1-14). Both reveals that ask for a port of exit use it — the transit reveal, where the field is named transitExitBorderControlPost, and the temporary-admission reveal, where it is named temporaryAdmissionPortOfExit — and both are fed by the same builder at app/routes.js:8763-8776, so Design release 1 uses one exit list rather than one per reason. Anything else is rejected with "Select a port of exit". The user is offered no other option. The ten are not a subset of the frontend's 78: entries such as "Heathrow Airport – Airpets Limited (animals)" have no counterpart in the ports-of-entry data at all, so this is a different list rather than a narrowing of the one Frontend already holds.

The port of exit has to become its own list of animal exit border control posts, labelled with their BCP codes, rather than a second use of the arrival ports. Frontend cannot do this alone: the ports service exposes one list and the reference-data service exposes only ports-of-entry, and the records carry a code and a name and nothing else, so there is no designation to filter on. A new endpoint and a new reference list are needed in trade-imports-reference-data, and the ports service needs a second accessor beside list(). Once that exists the frontend change is small — a different source for portItems and for the validation set in the same controller, and the hint sentence "Exit and entry share the same port list." comes out. Note for whoever schedules this: Frontend is not doing this by accident. It is following a different requirements source, the V4 field spec quoted in its own obligation, which says exit and entry share a list. Design release 1 is the signed-off design and says otherwise, so the two documents disagree and this ticket is where that gets settled.

FALSIFIED BY: A second port list in the frontend, or an exit filter over the one it has. src/server/app/services/ports/index.js exposes exactly one list, primed from one endpoint, and the port-of-exit select maps over it unfiltered; finding an exit-specific source would prove this wrong.

increments.title: Halfway through a new notification the frontend sends the user back to the hub and makes them start each remaining section from it, where Design release 1 carries straight on and runs the whole notification through in one sequence
increments.detail:
A new notification is walked through seven questions and then dropped on the hub. The sequence is origin, what are you importing, consignment details, main reason for importing, purpose in the internal market, animal identification and additional animal details (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39); pressing "Save and continue" on the last of them does not go to the arrival details, it goes to the hub, because the sequence has run out and the fall-through returns the hub path (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:41-53). From there the pattern repeats for the rest of the notification: every later section is entered from a task row and ends by returning to the hub, because the within-section next target also falls through to the hub when a section has no further page (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:27-37). The four sections still to answer at that point — documents, addresses, transport and the consignment contact (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:59-80) — are therefore four separate departures from the task list and four returns to it.

Design release 1 has one sequence and runs it end to end. Its steps are origin, what are you importing, reason for import, consignment details, animal identification where it applies, additional details, arrival details, transit countries where they apply, transporter, upload documents, roles and addresses, contact address, review and declaration (app/routes.js:1256-1285), and saving a page moves to the next step in that list (app/routes.js:1287-1305). Pressing "Save and continue" on the additional animal details takes the user to the arrival details (app/routes.js:9533). The hub is somewhere a user chooses to go — by pressing the secondary "Save and return to overview", or by opening the notification from the dashboard — not somewhere the journey puts them, so a user who follows the primary button reaches the declaration without seeing it.

Carry the sequence on past the additional animal details instead of ending it there, so "Save and continue" moves to the next question in the notification and the user reaches the review page in one pass. That means the opening run at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/run.js:22-39 stops being an opening run and becomes the whole journey, in Design release 1's order — arrival details, transit countries where they apply, transporter, upload documents, roles and addresses, contact address, then review — and the fall-through to the hub at :41-53 and at src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:36 applies only at the end of the journey rather than at the end of every section. The hub stays reachable throughout: both sides already put a secondary "Save and return to overview" button on each page, so nothing has to be added to get back to it. This is not the same change as unlocking the hub's rows (inc-032): that one decides what a user can start from the task list, this one decides whether they are sent to the task list at all.

FALSIFIED BY: Saving the frontend's additional-animal-details page and landing on a journey page rather than on the hub. This run's own frontend capture asserts the opposite — after the additional-details page is saved it asserts the URL is the bare journey path, which is the hub — so finding a redirect to /arrival-details or any other page there would prove this wrong.

increments.title: DR1 puts each commodity's identifier boxes in the order that commodity's own list gives; the frontend puts them in one fixed order for every animal, so a cow is asked for its passport before its ear tag.
increments.detail:
The boxes come out in the same order whatever animal is being identified, because the order is a property of the service rather than of the commodity: the identification copy block declares passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name in that sequence and the card renders whichever of them are in scope without resorting them (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/identifier/fields.js:21-30). On the captured cow the person is asked for Passport number, then Tattoo, then Ear tag number. The two free-text fallbacks are appended after the typed fields by the same rule.

DR1 asks for each commodity's identifiers in the order that commodity's own list sets, and the orders genuinely differ: cattle is Ear tag then Passport, a horse is Microchip, Passport, Horse name, and a cat, dog or ferret is Microchip, Passport, Tattoo (app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19). The panel simply loops the list it is handed, so the data is the order. On the captured cattle panel the person is asked for the ear tag first — the identifier a cow actually carries — and the passport second.

Move the identifier order off the copy block and onto the commodity, so each commodity carries its identifiers as an ordered list and the card renders them in that order. Two of the frontend's commodities disagree with DR1 today: a cow should read Ear tag then Passport where it currently reads Passport then Ear tag, and a horse should read Microchip, Passport, Horse name. This has to be settled before the microchip field is added, because a global order has nowhere to put a field that DR1 asks for first on some commodities and not at all on others, and after tattoo comes off cattle, because until then the cow panel has a third box in the middle of the pair.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding DR1's cattle panel render Passport above Ear tag, or finding the frontend sort a commodity's identifier fields by anything other than the order they are declared in the copy block.

increments.title: DR1 asks nothing at all about identifying a commodity that has no identifier type of its own; the frontend asks for free-text identification details and an animal description instead.
increments.detail:
Every commodity gets an identification record. Where the commodity is on none of the four identifier allowlists — of the five commodities the frontend offers, that is Fish — the record falls back to two free-text fields, 'Identification details' (hinted 'Any other way this animal is identified, if it has no passport, tattoo or ear tag') and 'Animal description'. fe-animal-identification-fish is that page: a salmon line headed 'Fish (0301) — Salmo salar', with those two boxes and no others, asking a person to say in prose how one fish out of a consignment is told from the next. The fallback obligations apply by the inverse gate at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:174-198, and the person must still enter one record per animal counted before the task can complete.

DR1 asks for identification only where the commodity has a typed identifier set. Ornamental fish carries an empty identifier list (app/data/commodities.js:281-284), so it gets no panel, and there is no free-text fallback anywhere in DR1. On a consignment where no commodity has identifiers the page does not exist for that person at all: the identification task row is dropped from the notification overview and a request for the page redirects on to additional details.

Two changes travel together and both are needed for the page to behave as DR1 does. Drop the identificationDetails and description obligations so a commodity with no typed identifier gets no fields, and make the identification page and its hub task row conditional on at least one commodity line having a typed identifier — today the page is always reachable and the unit-record count rule still demands one record per animal. Check what the at-least-one-identifier rule on the unit record means once the fallbacks are gone: a fish line would have no identifier obligation able to satisfy it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a free-text identification or description field rendered on any DR1 identification panel, or a DR1 identification panel rendered for a commodity whose identifier list is empty.

increments.title: The identification page's green button reads 'Save and finish' where every other page in both services reads 'Save and continue', and DR1 reads 'Save and continue' here too.
increments.detail:
At the foot of the identification page the green button reads 'Save and finish' — the only page in the service where it does not read 'Save and continue'. Every other journey page takes the shared macro's default (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:5); this page passes an override at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/animal-identification.njk:25, using the string at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:95. The button behaves like every other Save and continue: it saves whatever is in the open record and moves the person to the next page.

DR1's identification page ends with 'Save and continue', the same words as the rest of its journey, and does the same thing — it captures the open record for any single-animal species and moves on (app/views/animal-identification-details.html:144-148, handled at app/routes.js:10415-10423). DR1 keeps 'Save and finish' for a different job entirely: it is the in-panel button on the last outstanding animal of a species, meaning finish this species, not finish this page.

Change the identification page's primary button to 'Save and continue' and let it take the shared default, in English and Welsh. Small on its own, but it stops mattering less once identification--save-and-add-another-always-shown lands: that finding puts 'Save and finish' on the in-card button for the last outstanding record, and if the page-level button still says the same words the page would show two identically labelled buttons doing different things. Doing this one first, or with it, avoids that.

increments.title: The frontend shows 'Save and add another' on every identification record, including a consignment of one animal; DR1 hides it when there is one animal and calls it 'Save and finish' on the last.
increments.detail:
The button inside the record loop reads 'Save and add another' whatever is left to enter, and three captured states now say so. On a line of one animal the counter reads 'Enter details for Bos taurus 1 of 1' and the button still invites the person to add another. On a line of two with one already saved the counter reads 'Enter details for Bos taurus 2 of 2' — this is the last animal there is — and the button still reads 'Save and add another'. Only when the last record is saved does the wording stop being wrong, and that is because the whole entry block goes: the page then shows the saved records and the sentence 'You have entered details for all 2 Bos taurus animals'. So the words never tell the person what pressing them will do next. The button is rendered with no condition of its own at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/animal-identification/_identification-card.njk:71-76.

DR1 makes the in-panel button say what is actually left to do. Where the species has one animal there is no in-panel button at all and the page's own Save and continue captures the record; where more remain it reads 'Save and add another'; and on the last outstanding animal it reads 'Save and finish' (app/routes.js:1711-1722). The captured DR1 panel is two cattle with both outstanding, which is why it shows 'Save and add another'.

Make the in-card button reflect the records still to enter on that line: no button when the line's number of animals is one, 'Save and finish' when this is the last outstanding record, 'Save and add another' otherwise.
