increments.title: The frontend asks for a tattoo on every cow; DR1 asks a cow only for an ear tag and a passport.
increments.detail:
The cow identification record offers three fields in this order — Passport number, Tattoo, Ear tag number. Tattoo is there because Cow is on the tattoo allowlist alongside Cat and Dog (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:109), which gates the tattoo obligation at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:127-135.

DR1's cattle panel offers two fields, Ear tag then Passport. Tattoo is not on the cattle set at all — app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:9-12 gives commodity code 0102 exactly Ear tag and Passport, and Tattoo appears only under 01061900, the cat/dog/ferret code.

Remove Cow from the tattoo allowlist in the commodities stub so the tattoo obligation stops applying to cattle lines. Nothing else moves: tattoo stays in scope for cats and dogs, and the at-least-one-identifier rule on the unit record is still satisfiable for a cow through the ear tag or the passport. Any saved cow record already holding a tattoo value is orphaned by the change, so check whether stored answers need clearing when the obligation goes out of scope.

increments.title: The frontend asks whether the consignment holds unweaned animals when it holds horses; DR1 asks that question only of cattle and pigs.
increments.detail:
'Does the consignment contain any unweaned animals?' is rendered whenever any commodity line is a Cow or a Horse, and is mandatory when it is rendered. The rule is the two-name allowlist at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:117, read by the obligation at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/aggregates.js:46-55. A person importing horses alone is asked the question and cannot continue without answering it.

DR1 asks the question only where a selected commodity is one that carries unweaned options, and in DR1's catalogue that is cattle and pigs — not horses, and not sheep or goats (app/routes.js:1158-1183). A horses-only consignment reaches additional details and is asked what the animals are certified for and nothing else. The captured DR1 page shows the question because the consignment is cattle.

Correct the unweaned allowlist so it names the commodities DR1 asks the question of. Within the five commodities the frontend offers today that means dropping Horse and leaving Cow, which makes the question disappear from a horses-only consignment. Pig is on DR1's list but is not a commodity the frontend can express at all, so it can only be added once the commodity catalogue is filled out. The question's answer is already purged when it falls out of scope, so no separate cleanup is needed.

increments.title: DR1 puts the document being added, and the button that saves it, inside a bordered group headed "File upload"; the frontend runs the whole page as one flat column so nothing shows which button acts on the row in front of the user.
increments.detail:
The upload page is a single unbroken column: heading, Document reference, Date of issue, the file field, "Save and add another", the saved-documents table, then "Continue", "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-92). There is no heading, border or container of any kind between them, so "Save and add another" and "Continue" read as two buttons in the same list — on the populated page, two button rows a few centimetres apart with a table between them. A user cannot see from the page that the first acts on the fields above it and the second leaves the page — which is the difference that costs them the row they have typed.

The fields, "Save and add another" and the saved-documents table sit inside a bordered section headed "File upload", the heading carried in a grey title bar at the top of the panel and labelled to the group by aria-labelledby (app/views/upload-documents.html:92-240). The page-level actions — "Save and continue", "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" — sit outside the border, below it (:242-260). The grouping is what tells the user which button belongs to the document in front of them and which belongs to the page, and it holds on every state of the page: dr1-upload-documents shows the empty group, dr1-upload-documents-populated shows the saved row inside the same border.

Wrap the reference, type, date and attachment fields, the "Save and add another" button and the saved-documents table in a bordered group with an h2 of "File upload", and leave the page-level save actions outside it. Use a govuk-frontend container rather than a bespoke card — the summary-card border is the closest match already in the toolbox, and Design release 1 draws its own panel with prototype-only classes that should not be reproduced — and reference the h2 from the group so the grouping is announced as well as drawn. The heading is new user-facing copy and belongs in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js. Keep the reading order exactly as it is — fields, add button, table. No behaviour changes; this is layout and one heading.

increments.title: Design release 1 tells a trader which documents to attach before the upload form; the frontend goes straight to the form with no guidance at all
increments.detail:
Between the "Upload documents" heading and the first field there is nothing. The captured DOM of fe-documents goes from the h1 straight into the form and the Document reference label, and the whole page contains no paragraph of body copy, no bulleted list of document kinds, no details expander and no link out to GOV.UK guidance. The page's copy file holds no guidance keys of any kind either (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:1-25), so there is nothing waiting to be switched on. A trader arriving on the page is told what to type but never what to attach or why: the words ITAHC, licence, invoice and certificate appear nowhere on the frontend page outside the saved-documents table.

The page opens with three pieces of guidance before the form. First a paragraph: "You must attach an ITAHC if this consignment requires one. If you do not have it now, you can add it later. All documents should be uploaded before the consignment arrives at the UK port. Documents must be in English and you must upload all pages." Then "Other documents you may need to attach include:" over a bulleted list of "import licences or authorisations" and "commercial documents or invoices". Then a closed details expander, "Check which additional documents you must upload", holding a two-column table headed Consignment / Documents needed with three rows — animals that do not need a health certificate need an exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel; livestock transiting bluetongue restricted territories need Bluetongue declaration GBHC172; rodents imported for research purposes need an RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate — followed by "Check the documents you need on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)", linked to the GOV.UK import-of-products guidance. All of it is stated at app/views/upload-documents.html:37-79.

Add the guidance block to the frontend's documents template above the form: the intro paragraph, the "Other documents you may need to attach include" list, and a govukDetails expander holding the three-row table and the GOV.UK link. The copy belongs in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js and the markup in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:16-17, before the form element opens. This is content only — no new field, no validation, no service call — so it can be built today. The GOV.UK href in Design release 1 carries prototype analytics parameters — a _gl cross-domain linker value capturing one prototype session, which cannot be carried across at all — so use the clean guidance URL instead. One question is worth putting to a content designer rather than assuming: whether those three table rows are the settled content or a placeholder that will be replaced. Under the contract Design release 1 is the signed-off definition, so build the rows as they stand and treat any later rewrite as a later change. Raised as one finding rather than three because it is one block of page content that only makes sense together. It names no control deliberately: the difference is a block of prose above the form, not a field, and the whole-page shot is the right picture for it.

increments.title: DR1 asks the user to choose a document type from a list of thirteen before saving a document; the frontend never asks and guesses the type from the uploaded filename.
increments.detail:
The upload form asks for a document reference, a date of issue and a file, and nothing else (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:31-58). There is no document-type control anywhere on the page. Once the file is saved the type appears in the Document type column of the saved table, but the user never chose it: the controller derives it from the filename (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:109-112) by token-matching the filename against the document-types enum, longest match wins, falling back to OTHER when nothing matches. The module's own docstring states the rule outright — "The trader does not pick a type; the filename carries it" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/derive-document-type.js:3-18). A user who uploads scan001.pdf gets OTHER; a user who renames the same file itahc.pdf gets ITAHC. Nothing shows the guess before it is saved and nothing lets the user put it right afterwards — the only actions offered on a saved row are View file and Remove, and neither changes the type, so the only way out of a wrong guess is to remove the document and upload it again under a different filename. The obligation model already declares accompanyingDocumentType mandatory for every document (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:30-35), so a field the model requires has no surface at all.

Between Document reference and Date of issue the card carries a Document type select labelled "Document type" (app/views/upload-documents.html:115-130). increments.title: Design release 1 lets a trader drop a document onto the page and shows which file is chosen; the frontend offers only the browser's own file button
increments.detail:
The file control is a bare input rendered by the standard file-upload component with no JavaScript enhancement (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:51-58). What the trader sees on fe-documents is whatever the browser draws for a file input — on the capture, a small grey "Choose File" button with "No file chosen" beside it, in the browser's own type rather than the service's. There is no drop target, so a file cannot be dragged onto the page, and the chosen filename is shown only in the browser's own text beside the button, in the browser's own wording and without being announced to a screen reader.

The control is a dashed-outline drop zone occupying the width of the card. Inside it a status line, in a highlighted band and marked aria-live="polite", reads "No file chosen" until a file is picked and then reads the file's name; below that a styled "Choose file" button sits beside the words "or drop file" (app/views/upload-documents.html:172-179). A trader can drag a document from their desktop onto the zone, and either way the page itself tells them which file they are about to upload. The zone also takes an error style of its own when the attachment fails validation, its dashed border turning red, so the failure is drawn on the control the trader has to go back to.

Turn on the JavaScript-enhanced file upload for this control. The frontend is on govuk-frontend 6.3, whose file upload component provides exactly this behaviour — a drop zone, a "Choose file" button, the words "or drop file" and a live region naming the chosen file — when the component is asked for it and its JavaScript is initialised. That is a change to the govukFileUpload call at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:51-58 plus initialising the component in the page's client bundle at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/client/index.js. The zone's own error state comes with the component, and the unenhanced input stays behind it as the no-JavaScript fallback, so nothing is taken away from a trader whose JavaScript does not run. Design release 1 hand-built the same thing in the prototype's own markup, so the requirement is the behaviour, not the bespoke classes; the design-system component satisfies it and should be used instead of rebuilding one.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a drop target, or any element carrying the text "or drop file", in the captured DOM of fe-documents. Its file control is a single input.govuk-file-upload with no surrounding wrapper and no live region.

increments.title: Frontend caps a notification at 10 accompanying documents; Design release 1 allows 15
increments.detail:
A notification may hold at most ten documents. The cap is an obligation on the documents group (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:24-27) and the page reads it from there (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/contracts/max-documents.js:3). A trader who chooses an eleventh file is refused on submit, with an error summary reading "You can add a maximum of 10 documents" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:73).

Design release 1 allows fifteen. That number backs the validation, which refuses a sixteenth with "You can upload a maximum of 15 files" (app/routes.js:9106-9109) — a check that short-circuits every other validation on the page and returns that one message, anchored to the attachment field (app/routes.js:9103-9112) — and it is also the number stated in the hint above the upload control (app/views/upload-documents.html:168).

Raise the cap from 10 to 15 at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:25. That one value is read by the page, the Add affordance and the error message, so nothing else has to move: the error copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:73 already interpolates the number. Whether that message keeps the frontend's word "documents" or takes Design release 1's "files" is settled by the validation-wording finding at inc-143, not here. Update the obligation file's own header comment with it, which describes the group as 0..10 at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:2-16. This lands entirely in Frontend and the band is frontend-work: the cap is a frontend obligation constant and has no counterpart on the wire — its only non-test uses are the error message and the submit guard, and no other service is told the number. Stating the limit on the page before a trader chooses a file is a separate change, raised as documents--document-limit-not-stated-before-a-file-is-chosen. The two are independently schedulable in either order: the frontend could state its current limit of ten today without touching the cap, and the cap could be raised without the page ever mentioning it.

increments.title: The frontend rejects any document over 10 MB; Design release 1 allows files up to 50MB
increments.detail:
The upload control's hint reads "Your file must be:" over two bullets, the first of which is "smaller than 10 MB". The limit is enforced twice — in the browser, from a data-max-file-size attribute of 10000000 on the form element, and on the server, where a file over the limit is refused with "The selected file must be smaller than 10 MB" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/form/errors.js:34-36). The route's own payload cap, MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, is set just above the file limit so that an oversize post is caught and answered rather than silently dropped (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-49). Ten decimal megabytes is a deliberate choice made against the platform rather than against the design: the code says so, at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-46, where the comment records that the value stays clear of the 10 MiB nginx ingress cap on the hosting platform. So a trader with a 20 MB scanned health certificate cannot attach it and is given no alternative on the page.

The same hint list opens with "files that are smaller than 50MB" (app/views/upload-documents.html:166). Design release 1 states 50MB as the ceiling a trader may upload to, and repeats the bullet in every error state of the page.

Raise the accepted file size from 10 MB to 50MB and change the hint bullet and the oversize error message to match. The value and its label live in one place, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:40-46, MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES has to move with it, and the browser-side check reads the same number from the form's data-max-file-size attribute, so the frontend edit is small. It is banded needs-backend because the frontend cannot make the change alone: the code records that 10 MB was chosen to stay under the platform's 10 MiB ingress limit, so the request-body cap on the hosting platform's ingress and on whatever receives the upload has to be raised to at least 50MB first, otherwise a large file will be rejected by the infrastructure before the service sees it and the trader will get a platform error page instead of a validation message. That is roughly a fivefold increase on the ingress ceiling in force today and nothing in the frontend establishes that the platform will allow it, so confirm the ceiling with the document-upload service before changing the number. Settle the unit in the same edit — Design release 1 writes "50MB" with no space where the frontend writes "10 MB" with one.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a data-max-file-size attribute other than 10000000 on the form in the captured DOM of fe-documents, or a hint bullet on that page that names a limit other than 10 MB.

increments.detail:
The page offers two ways to submit the document form and only one of them keeps anything. "Save and add another" posts action=add and saves the document. "Continue" posts action=continue from inside the same form, so the reference, the date of issue and the chosen file all travel to the server in that request — and the server never looks at them. The post handler branches on the action and reads the payload only for add and remove; every other action loads the page state fresh, checks whether any already-saved document is still being scanned, and redirects to the next page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279). Nothing is saved, no error is shown, and the next screen gives no sign that anything was dropped. A trader who fills the three fields, chooses their health certificate and presses the primary green button — the one the whole rest of the journey has taught them to press — arrives at the next page having attached nothing. "Save and return to hub" behaves the same way.

"Save and continue" completes the document. Design release 1 treats a part-filled form as an intention to attach: if the trader has chosen a document type, it validates the whole form, and either adds the document to the notification and moves on, or stays on the page and shows the same four messages the add path would have shown — "Enter a document reference", "Select a document type", "Enter a date of issue" and "Upload a document" — so the trader is told what is missing rather than losing the file (app/routes.js:10173-10193). The captured Save and continue refusal is that state, showing the three messages that remain once the type has been chosen. The chosen type is the whole of the signal: the branch is entered only when the posted document type is one of the valid options, so a trader who fills in the reference, the date and the attachment but leaves the select on "Select one" is carried forward with the row dropped exactly as the frontend drops it. Uploading remains optional — an untouched form continues without complaint. "Save and return to overview" is the one action that deliberately discards a part-filled form.

Make Continue finish the document rather than throw it away. On a Continue post, look at the add-a-document fields: if the trader has entered anything at all, run the same validation the Add path runs and either save the document and move on, or re-render the page with the field errors. The branch is in the post dispatcher at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279, which today falls through to the redirect for every action that is not add or remove; the saving path it needs already exists as postAdd at :92-129 and needs no new validation, no new copy and no service change. Two decisions belong to whoever picks this up. First, what counts as "the trader meant to attach something": Design release 1 keys it on the document type being chosen, and the frontend has no document type until documents--document-type-not-asked lands, so until then key it on any of the three fields being non-empty — an interim rule that is stricter than Design release 1, which would carry a trader on when only a reference has been typed, and it should be recorded as an extrapolation rather than as Design release 1's requirement. Second, whether "Save and return to hub" should behave the same way — Design release 1 says no, and matching it exactly means only Continue changes.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding that a Continue post reaches the frontend's document-saving path. Follow action=continue through the post dispatcher at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279: if it reaches postAdd, or reads payload.file, payload.accompanyingDocumentReference or payload.accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue anywhere before redirecting, this finding is wrong.

increments.title: Design release 1 tells a trader that ZIP files are not allowed and why; the frontend refuses them silently and gives a message that never mentions ZIP
increments.detail:
The file-requirements hint says nothing about archives. Headed "Your file must be:", it has two bullets — a size and a list of accepted types — and the word ZIP appears nowhere on the page. A ZIP file is in fact refused, because the accepted types are an allow-list of eight extensions (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/upload-config.js:3-18) applied both as the file input's accept attribute and as a server-side check, but the trader who tries one is told only "The selected file must be a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX", and only after they have chosen the file. Somebody who has zipped several certificates together to save uploads is left to infer the rule and is given no reason for it.

The fourth bullet of the file-requirements hint reads "ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons" (app/views/upload-documents.html:169), stated before the trader chooses a file and giving the reason as well as the rule. It is on the page on dr1-upload-documents and on every error state of the page.

Add "ZIP files are not allowed for security reasons" as a bullet in the file-requirements hint under "Your file must be:", in Design release 1's words, in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js beside the existing file hint keys at :11-16 and rendered from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-48. Copy only — the behaviour is already correct, since the allow-list already excludes ZIP.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the string "ZIP" anywhere in the captured DOM of fe-documents. It does not appear, in the hint, the accept attribute or the error copy.

increments.title: Frontend never tells a trader how many documents a notification may hold until they hit the limit; Design release 1 states it in the file requirements above the upload control
increments.detail:
Nothing on the documents page says how many documents a notification may hold. The captured DOM of fe-documents and fe-documents-populated states exactly two requirements above the upload control — that a file must be "smaller than 10 MB" and that it must be "a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-48) — and no count appears anywhere on either page. A trader learns the limit only by reaching it, at which point the error summary tells them (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:73), anchored to the saved-documents table rather than to the form (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/form/errors.js:52-57), after they have already chosen a file and tried to upload it. The Add affordance is not hidden at the cap either, so there is no silent signal in place of the missing sentence.

Design release 1 states the count as one of the four requirements in the hint above the upload control, alongside the size and the file types: "up to a maximum of 15 files" (app/views/upload-documents.html:168). A trader is told before they choose anything, and told again if they reach the limit, so the number is stated twice on the page rather than only at the point of refusal.

Add the document count as a bullet in the file-requirements hint at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:43-48, so the page states the limit before a trader picks a file rather than after. The copy belongs beside the existing size and file-type bullets in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js. This is copy on a page Frontend already has and it needs nothing else to land first, so the band is frontend-work. It is independent of the cap's value: the sentence can be written against whatever the obligation currently allows, and if documents--max-documents-cap lands first the sentence says fifteen instead of ten. Write it to read from the same obligation value the error message reads rather than hard-coding a number, so the two can never disagree.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any statement of a document count limit in the file-requirements hint of the captured DOM of fe-documents or fe-documents-populated. That hint has exactly two bullets and neither mentions a count.

increments.title: The documents page and the consignment addresses hub end with a button reading "Continue"; Design release 1 reads "Save and continue" on both, and reads "Continue" only on check your answers and the declaration
increments.detail:
Almost every journey page ends with a primary button reading "Save and continue", which is what the shared button macro renders when a page passes no primary of its own (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:5, reading src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:43). Four pages pass their own primary and label it just "Continue", and between them they account for twelve of the sixty-seven captured frontend screens: the accompanying-documents page in all four of its captured states (fe-documents, fe-documents-populated, fe-documents-scanning, fe-documents-error), the consignment addresses hub in all three (fe-addresses-hub, fe-addresses-hub-empty, fe-addresses-hub-complete), check your answers in all three (fe-check-answers, fe-check-answers-incomplete, fe-check-answers-submitted) and the declaration in both (fe-declaration, fe-declaration-error). The two overrides that matter are src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:92 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:16, each reading a per-feature copy key set to the string "Continue" at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:51 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:8. On both of those pages the "Continue" button sits immediately to the left of a secondary button reading "Save and return to hub", so the page offers the user a choice between a button that says it saves and a button that does not.

Design release 1 ends the same two pages with "Save and continue". Upload documents states it at app/views/upload-documents.html:245 and the consignment addresses hub at app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:114, and both render it beside a secondary "Save and return to overview". Design release 1 does use a bare "Continue" — but only on two pages, and they are the two at the end of the journey where there is nothing left to save: review your notification (app/views/review-notification.html:184) and the declaration (app/views/declaration.html:91), each of which ends with that single button and no secondary. Across the sixty captured Design release 1 screens the primary reads "Save and continue" on forty-five and "Continue" on seven, and those seven are review notification and its incomplete state, the declaration and its error state, add a transporter, the contact address for the consignment, and add an address to the address book.

Change the two per-feature copy keys from "Continue" to "Save and continue": src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:51 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:8. The documents override must stay in place because it also carries name="action" and value="continue", which the post dispatcher branches on; only its text changes. The addresses override carries nothing else, so that page can drop its primary argument at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:16 and fall through to the macro's default instead. Seven captured screens change: the four documents states and the three addresses hub states. FIVE MUST NOT CHANGE. Check your answers and the declaration already read "Continue" on both sides, because Design release 1 reads "Continue" there too — so fe-check-answers, fe-check-answers-incomplete, fe-check-answers-submitted, fe-declaration and fe-declaration-error are already right and renaming them would introduce a difference that does not exist today. This is not a service-wide rename; it is two copy keys. Two boundaries with neighbouring findings, because a corpus-wide duplicate sweep has already run and this is a new near-neighbour. First: service-wide--save-and-cancel-buttons-name-the-hub renames the two controls to the RIGHT of this button — "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub" — which come from the shared keys at src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:42-45 and change on every page at once. This finding is the button to their left, which comes from each page's own copy and changes on two pages. Different strings, different files, different blast radius. Second: documents--continue-discards-a-filled-in-document says that pressing this button on the documents page throws away a document the trader has filled in but not added. These two must land together or the copy one must land second, because renaming the button to "Save and continue" while it still discards makes the label state something untrue. One further difference runs the other way and is already recorded elsewhere: on two pages Design release 1 reads "Continue" where the frontend reads "Save and continue" — the contact address page and the transporter-type page — and that is inside service-wide--save-and-cancel-shown-where-the-design-shows-one-button, whose own screens are those pages and whose change removes the surrounding controls at the same time. It is deliberately not folded in here.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a primary submit button whose text is exactly "Save and continue" in the captured DOM of dr1-upload-documents or dr1-roles-and-addresses, or one whose text is exactly "Continue" in the captured DOM of fe-documents or fe-addresses-hub — either would mean the two sides agree on the pages this finding says they disagree on.

increments.title: The frontend accepts a .jpg file but leaves JPG out of the list of accepted file types it shows the trader; Design release 1 lists it
increments.detail:
The second bullet of the file-requirements hint reads "a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, PNG, XLS or XLSX" — seven types, with JPG absent. increments.title: The frontend labels a document's virus-check status "Checking" and "Safe"; Design release 1 labels the same two states "Scanning for virus" and "Check completed"
increments.detail:
The Status column of the saved-documents table shows a tag per document. While the scan runs it is a blue tag reading "Checking" and once the scan clears it is a green tag reading "Safe" — both captured, on fe-documents-scanning, whose two rows show one of each. Two further states exist behind the same mechanism: "Virus found" when the scan fails and "Unknown" when the status cannot be read. The words come from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:52-57 and are applied at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/view-model/fragments/status.js:7-24. Neither of the two shared labels says what Design release 1's says: "Checking" does not name what is being checked, and "Safe" is a verdict about the file where Design release 1's is a statement about the check. The tag carries no other text, so a screen-reader user hears "Safe" with nothing saying what is safe or what was checked.

The same column, the same two colours, different words: a blue tag reading "Scanning for virus" while the check runs and a green tag reading "Check completed" once it has (app/routes.js:9082-9083). Each tag is preceded by visually hidden text naming the document it belongs to — "Virus check status for ITAHC-000123" (app/views/upload-documents.html:217-224) — so the status is unambiguous when read out.

Change the two scan-status tag labels to Design release 1's wording — PENDING becomes "Scanning for virus" and COMPLETE becomes "Check completed" — at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:52-57, and in the Welsh copy file alongside it. The same words are also embedded in the page's client-side polling payload, which is generated from the same copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/view-model/fragments/status.js:26-29, so the live-updating tag changes with it and needs no separate edit. While in the same cell, add the visually hidden "Virus check status for {reference}" prefix Design release 1 puts before each tag. The frontend's two further states, "Virus found" and "Unknown", have no counterpart in Design release 1 and are left alone.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the words "Scanning for virus" or "Check completed" in the captured DOM of fe-documents-scanning. Its two tags read "Safe" and "Checking", and the same two words appear again in the page's data-scan-copy payload.

increments.detail:
The page's messages are held in one copy file (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/copy/copy.en.js:63-81). A blank date of issue gives "Enter the date of issue"; an unparseable one gives "Enter a real date of issue"; a missing file gives "Select a file to upload"; going over the cap gives "You can add a maximum of 10 documents". Each message is used twice, once in the error summary and once against the field, so each is a single string doing both jobs.

The rendered summary on dr1-upload-documents-error lists all four row errors verbatim, dr1-upload-documents-continue-error lists the three that remain once a type has been chosen, and dr1-upload-documents-limit-error carries the capacity one alone.

Bring the four differing messages to DR1's wording: "Enter a date of issue", "Enter a real date", "Upload a document", and "You can upload a maximum of {max} files", in both language copy files, and update the tests that assert the current strings. increments.title: Frontend makes a trader pick the importer and place of destination from scratch; Design release 1 offers a one-click "Same as consignee" and "Same as place of origin"
increments.detail:
Every unanswered row on the Consignment addresses page offers one action, "Add", which opens that party's picker. There is no way to reuse an address already chosen for another party: the row's action list holds a single link built from the party's slug (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:37-45), and no captured frontend screen or state contains the string "Same as". The page even carries the hint that invites the shortcut — the Importer row reads "This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed." — and then offers no way to say "the same". A trader whose importer, consignee and place of destination are one company searches the book and picks the same row three times.

Design release 1 puts a second action beside "Add" on exactly the rows where a copy makes sense, and only once there is something to copy. When a consignee has been chosen, the Importer and Place of destination rows each gain a "Same as consignee" control; when a place of origin has been chosen, the Consignor row gains "Same as place of origin" (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:83-101, availability decided at app/routes.js:2118-2133). Pressing it fills that row in place, from the same page, with no picker in between; the row then shows the copied address and a "Change" link like any other.

Add a copy-from-another-party action to the Consignment addresses page: "Same as place of origin" on the Consignor row, "Same as consignee" on the Importer and Place of destination rows, each shown only when the source party has been answered and the target has not. It submits the hub's own form rather than navigating, so the trader stays on the page. The frontend's hub is already a POST form with a hidden crumb (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/template.njk:11-15) and the parties table already carries the ids the copy needs (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:20-57), so nothing has to land first. Note that place of origin is stored inline while consignor, consignee, importer and destination are stored as references (`inline: true` at :26), so copying the place of origin onto the consignor must copy the record, not the reference. `controls` names "Same as place of origin" rather than "Same as consignee" because the second occurs twice on its capture and would be refused a crop; the two controls are the same change.

increments.title: Frontend's consignment addresses list shows only the chosen party's name; Design release 1 shows the whole address the trader picked
increments.detail:
Once a party has been chosen, the Consignment addresses page shows the party's name and nothing else. In the captured answered state the five rows read "Astra Rosales", "Tech Imports Ltd", "Origin Farm", "British Livestock Ltd" and "Import Co UK", each beside a "Change" link, with no street, town, postcode or country anywhere on the page. The row value is the record's name alone (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:32-53, which passes `parties[party.id]?.name` as the summary-list value at :49). A trader who has picked the wrong record of two with similar names cannot tell from this page; to check it they have to reopen the picker, because nothing else in the addresses section shows the address again. It reappears only on the check-your-answers page at the end of the journey, which does render every party as a name and a full address.

Design release 1 prints the selected address in full inside an inset block under each party heading — the name in bold, then every address line, then the postcode and country on the last line, then "Change" (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:59-68). In the captured answered state Place of origin reads Green Valley Farm / Str. Principală nr. 45 / Sat Sânpetru / Comuna Sânpetru / Jud. Brașov / 507190, Romania. The CPH row uses the same inset and prints the number.

Show the selected address, not just the name, in every answered row of the Consignment addresses page: name, then the address lines, then postcode and country. The data is already in reach — the picker's own "View details" expander renders exactly these lines from `detailLines` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:15-22) and the hub already resolves the full party record before rendering (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:55-59). Nothing else has to land first. Note that the frontend's rows are a govuk summary list and Design release 1's are headed sections with an inset; the requirement is that the address is visible, not that the component matches. `controls` is deliberately empty: the difference runs down all six rows of the page, and the only named control on a row, "Change", occurs six times and would be refused a crop anyway.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any address line, town, postcode or country rendered in an answered row of the frontend's Consignment addresses page. The captured DOM of fe-addresses-hub-complete contains none of the address text for any of its six answered rows.

increments.title: Frontend's Consignment addresses page offers every unanswered party a link reading just "Add"; Design release 1 names the party in the link — "Add a place of origin", "Add a consignor"
increments.detail:
Every unanswered row on the Consignment addresses page carries one link and it reads "Add". The party is appended only as visually hidden text, so a sighted trader scanning the page meets six identical links reading "Add", one under each of Place of origin, Consignor or exporter, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination and County Parish Holding number (CPH). The string is one shared word for every row (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:6-7), applied at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:41 with the row title pushed into visuallyHiddenText at :42.

Design release 1 gives each row its own link text naming what is being added: "Add a place of origin", "Add a consignor", "Add a consignee", "Add an importer", "Add a place of destination" and "Add a CPH number". Each is a designed string held against the section it belongs to (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:6, :19, :33, :46, :60, :74) and rendered as the row's only link (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:104-106). Nothing is hidden: what a screen reader announces and what a sighted trader reads are the same words.

Give each unanswered row a link that names its party, using Design release 1's six strings, instead of the shared word "Add" with the party hidden. This is one new string per party in the addresses copy — the party table already holds a title per party at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:20-57, so the link text can sit beside it — plus the CPH row's own string, and the Welsh counterparts. The visuallyHiddenText on the action then becomes redundant and should be dropped rather than doubled up. This is deliberately only about the unanswered rows: what an answered row shows is a separate and larger change, raised as addresses--hub-shows-only-the-party-name.

increments.title: DR1 collects the CPH number as three boxes sized to its county, parish and holding parts; the frontend takes the whole number in one free-text field.
increments.detail:
One govukInput at width-10 takes the whole number (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/template.njk:11-23). fe-cph-number shows a single empty box with nothing to say how the nine digits divide up. On submit the controller strips slashes and checks for exactly nine digits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:75-80,32-40), so "123456789", "12/345/6789" and "1/2/3456789" are all accepted and stored identically; a trader who mistypes a digit in the wrong part gets no signal, because nothing on the page knows which part is which. What the page does say about the shape is wrong. The hint under the box reads "For example, 123456789 or 123/456/789." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/copy/copy.en.js:5), and its second example teaches a 3/3/3 grouping that no CPH number uses: a county parish holding number is two digits of county, three of parish and four of holding. The error never surfaces in testing, because the controller strips the slashes before counting digits (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:77), so a trader who copies the pattern still passes validation. The casualty is the trader who comes away believing their own number is wrongly formatted, or who transcribes it into the wrong grouping somewhere else.

DR1 uses a three-part input under the legend "CPH number" — County at width-2 and maxlength 2, Parish at width-3 and maxlength 3, Holding number at width-4 and maxlength 4, each numeric (app/views/partials/cph-number-input.html:17-53). dr1-cph-number shows the three boxes stepping up in width, which teaches the 2/3/4 shape without a word of copy. The parts post separately and are joined with slashes into "12/345/6789" when stored; the answered hub shows that slashed form (dr1-roles-and-addresses-complete). Each box carries its own label — County, Parish, Holding number — present for screen readers but clipped out of sight by the prototype's own stylesheet, so what a sighted trader meets is three boxes whose widths and hint carry the format between them. That hint is DR1's own, "For example 12/345/6789" (app/views/partials/cph-number-input.html:14), placed above all three boxes so that it explains the whole number rather than any one part, and the 2/3/4 shape it teaches is the shape the boxes enforce through their widths and maxlengths (:21,33,45).

Split the field into County, Parish and Holding number, sized 2/3/4 with numeric input modes and per-part maxlengths, and join them in the controller so the stored value stays the nine bare digits the backend already receives — the wire contract does not move. Validate each part for its own length so the error names the part that is wrong. Note that DR1 itself validates nothing on this page: the 2/3/4 shape rests on the maxlength attributes, so the frontend's nine-digit check is the stricter behaviour and should be kept. Take DR1's labels rather than its picture: three unlabelled boxes under one legend would be worse than the single field they replace. Correct the example at the same time, to the real grouping, "For example 12/345/6789", keeping the unslashed alternative only if content design wants it and making it consistent with the grouping if so. That one string is a fix in its own right and does not have to wait for the three boxes — it is a copy change with no validation work behind it — and while it stands the service goes on teaching a grouping that does not exist.

FALSIFIED BY: GDS content or accessibility guidance for this service ruling against splitting a single reference number across three boxes — the argument that applies to a National Insurance number — in which case the single field is right and only the hint is wrong.

increments.title: Frontend shows the four means of transport as radios, all visible at once; Design release 1 hides them inside a "Select one" dropdown
increments.detail:
"Means of transport to the port of entry" is a fieldset legend over four radios — Airplane, Railway, Road Vehicle, Vessel — all four visible on the page without interacting with anything, and none of them preselected (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:29-39).

The same question is a label over a dropdown. The closed control shows "Select one" and the four options — the same four, in the same order, with the same words — appear only when it is opened (app/views/arrival-details.html:110-119).

Change the means-of-transport control from a radio group to a select whose first, selected option reads "Select one". The option set, the wording of the options, their order and the label above them are already identical, so the control is the only thing that changes. This is the one finding in the transport slice where the frontend is closer to the GOV.UK Design System's advice than Design release 1 is — the Design System steers a four-option question towards radios — so a reviewer meeting this row should expect it to look backwards and should still read it as written: Design release 1 shows a dropdown here and the frontend does not.

increments.title: Opening the arrival date calendar drops it on top of the next two questions; Design release 1 opens it in the flow of the page so nothing is covered
increments.detail:
The calendar floats. It is positioned over the page and the rest of the form stays where it was, so the open dialog lands across "Port of entry" and "Means of transport to the port of entry": in the captured screenshot the port hint is sliced in half by the calendar's edge, the port field is hidden behind it, and only the tail of one "Vessel" radio shows below. A trader who opens the calendar to check a date can no longer see the two questions they were about to answer, and has to close it to get them back. The frontend takes the Ministry of Justice date picker exactly as the package ships it — `src/client/stylesheets/application.scss:2` imports the component's own stylesheet and adds nothing, and the page calls the macro unadorned at `src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.njk:16` — and that component's default is an overlay.

Design release 1 opens the same calendar in the flow of the page. increments.title: Frontend's arrival date hint spells out the earliest and latest date the user may enter; Design release 1's hint gives a worked example of the date format instead
increments.detail:
Under "Arrival date at port of entry" the hint reads "The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. Enter a date between {earliest} and {latest}." — the second sentence names both ends of the accepted window, computed from today (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:6-7, filled in at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/port-of-entry/port-of-entry.controller.js:97-101). It shows the user the boundaries but never shows them what a date should look like.

Under the same label the hint reads "The expected date of arrival at the port of entry. For example, 27/3/2026" (app/views/partials/arrival-date-picker.html:13). The second sentence is a worked example of the format, not a range, and it does not move.

Replace the second sentence of the arrival date hint with a worked example of the date format. The dates inside the two sentences are not what differs — both services derive the same seven-days-back, six-months-forward window from the clock, and both drive the date picker's bounds from it, so the window itself is unchanged. What differs is what the sentence is for: Design release 1 tells the user how to write a date, the frontend tells them which dates are allowed. Whether the range should still be stated anywhere is a copy decision that follows from adopting Design release 1's wording; the date picker already refuses out-of-range days and the frontend already has an out-of-range error message for the typed case (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:34-35). increments.title: DR1 builds the transit-country list one country at a time through a type-ahead, showing what has been added with a Remove link against each; the frontend renders all thirty-one countries as checkboxes and asks the user to find theirs by eye.
increments.detail:
The page renders every country in the list as a small checkbox — thirty-one of them, Austria through Switzerland — under the legend "Select all countries the consignment will travel through" and the hint "Select up to 12 countries" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transit-countries/transit-countries.njk:18-24). A user scrolls the whole list to find each country, and once boxes are ticked the only record of what was chosen is the ticks themselves, scattered down the page. The twelve-country cap is enforced on submit, so a user who ticks thirteen finds out after submitting.

DR1 asks "Enter a country", hinted "Enter each country that the consignment will travel through", with a single search box placeholdered "Search for a country" (app/views/transit-countries.html:56-110). Choosing a match adds the country to a summary table headed Country, one row each, with a Remove link (:119-139), and clears the search ready for the next. A user types three letters instead of scanning thirty-one options, and reads back what they have chosen as a short list rather than as ticks in a long one. The same twelve-country cap applies, but DR1 reaches it differently: the search box and its button are disabled once twelve are added, and a screen-reader message says "Maximum of 12 countries reached. Remove a country to add another." (app/assets/javascripts/transit-country-search.js:6, 160-172).

Replace the checkbox list with a type-ahead over the same country list plus a table of what has been added, one row per country with a Remove link. Keep the cap at twelve — DR1 caps at twelve too, so the cap is not the difference — but move how it is expressed: DR1 does not state it up front, it disables the search once the twelfth country is added and announces the limit. Design release 1 also announces each addition to assistive technology as it happens, so the new control needs a live region rather than only a visible row. Whether the frontend keeps its "Select up to 12 countries" hint alongside that is a copy choice; the control change is the work.

increments.title: Frontend refuses to leave the transit countries page until at least one country is chosen; Design release 1 treats the list as optional and lets a road or rail consignment through with none
increments.detail:
The question is compulsory once it applies. `transitedCountries` is in scope and mandatory whenever the means of transport is rail or a road vehicle (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:92-105), so a trader who presses Save and continue without ticking a box gets the page back with "There is a problem" and the message "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through", both in the error summary and above the checkbox list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:55). The notification cannot be submitted until a country is chosen, because the transit-countries task row has to be fulfilled like every other in-scope row.

Design release 1 asks the same question of the same traders and accepts no answer to it. Its transit-countries handler runs no validation of any kind: it clears any errors, saves whatever was posted — including an empty list — and moves on (app/routes.js:10533-10537). Its completeness check for the section is a function that returns a literal true with the comment "Transit countries are optional — any saved list (including empty) is acceptable" (app/routes.js:1932-1935), and the section is absent from the ten predicates that gate submission. So a road or rail consignment reaches the declaration with no transit country recorded, and nothing anywhere tells the trader one was expected.

Make the transit-countries answer optional. In src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:92-105 the in-scope branch keeps `inScope: true` and its reason but drops `status: 'mandatory'`, so the question is still asked of rail and road consignments and still purged for the others, but an empty selection no longer holds the task row out of fulfilled and no longer blocks submission. The "Select at least one country the consignment will travel through" message then has nothing to fire on and goes with it, along with the error state of the page. Nothing has to land first — the obligation and its copy are both frontend files, and the notification contract already carries an empty list. Note that this is a change to whether the question must be answered, not to how it is asked: replacing the checkbox list with a search-and-add control is transport--transit-countries-is-a-checkbox-list, and that work should carry this rule rather than the current one.

FALSIFIED BY: A validation error on Design release 1's transit-countries page after pressing Save and continue with no country chosen. Design release 1's captured page could only be photographed in its unanswered and answered states, so this is the one observation that would settle it, and the handler at app/routes.js:10533-10537 has no branch that could produce one.

increments.title: Frontend asks which type of transporter is moving the animals before showing any list; Design release 1 shows one searchable list of all approved transporters, commercial and private together, and asks the type only when a user adds a new one
increments.detail:
The transporter section opens on a page that begins with the DAERA and APHA authorisation guidance and only then asks the question. Below that guidance sits the heading "What type of transporter will move the animals?", hinted "We will ask for the transporter's details next.", with two radios, Commercial ("A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list") and Private ("You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address"). The answer forks the journey: Commercial goes to a list of approved commercial transporters to pick one from, Private goes to a blank name-and-address form. The two branches never meet, so a user whose transporter is already known to the service but is a private one has no list to pick it from and types the whole address again. The order and the fork are declared as three consecutive pages in one section at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:67-76, and the copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61.

The transporter section opens on one page headed "Transporter details", introduced "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.", carrying the same DAERA and APHA guidance apart from the wording and destination of its guidance link, then "Select a transporter" over a searchable table of every transporter the trader can use. The table mixes both kinds: Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd, Danish Meat Export ApS and Portuguese Livestock Lda are typed Commercial, and Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, Romanian Agri Exports SRL, Slovak Farm Export and Finnish Livestock Oy are typed Private. A user picks a row and continues. Only a user who cannot find their transporter presses "Add a transporter", and only then is the type question asked, on a separate page headed "Choose a transporter type" warned "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first." (app/views/transporter-add.html:32-36). The linear journey holds one transporter step, /transporter (app/routes.js:1274); both add pages sit off it.

Restructure the transporter section so the list comes first and the type question comes second. The frontend needs one transporter page that lists every transporter available to the trader, commercial and private, with the DAERA and APHA guidance and the "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment" introduction on it, and a route off that page for adding one that is not listed. Concretely, that means reversing the order of the task: `/transporters`, the route that asks the type today, becomes the list page — a search over the transporters the service knows about, one row per record showing its type, with a radio to pick one — and the commercial-or-private question moves behind an "Add a transporter" button beneath the table, as the first step of adding a record that is not on the list. The type chooser then moves off the linear journey onto that add route, asked only of a trader who could not find their transporter in the list, and the two branches it forks into become the two ways of adding a transporter rather than the two ways of choosing one. The words on the chooser and on the private form it leads to also change, and that is raised separately as transport--transporter-type-chooser-copy-differs so it can land on the pages as they stand today without waiting for this. This is the parent of five other transport findings and should land before them: the list needs a search box, the list needs Type and Status per row, the add route needs a commercial form, the chooser needs Design release 1's copy, and a transporter a user types in by hand needs somewhere to live so it can be picked again next time. Nothing outside the frontend has to change first for the restructuring itself — the list is a local fixture at src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29 and it can be widened to carry private transporters there.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a route in the frontend that reaches a combined transporter list before the type question is asked, or finding that Design release 1's /transporter table filters to one type once a transporter type has been chosen.

increments.title: Frontend's transporter authorisation guidance sends the user to a different GOV.UK page from the one Design release 1 sends them to, and words two of its lines differently
increments.detail:
The transporter authorisation guidance opens the transporter type page: the lead sentence about DAERA and APHA, three bullets, a guidance link, and two closing sentences. The link reads "Find out how to transport animals in connection with an economic activity (opens in new tab)" and goes to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/transporting-animals-in-great-britain, which is the general page on transporting animals in Great Britain. The last sentence reads "Documents issued in any EU Member State are not valid for use in GB." The whole block is one copy object at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:62-77, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters/transporters.njk:8-18.

Design release 1 shows the same guidance, in the same order, at the top of its transporter page (app/views/transporter.html:48-62). The lead sentence and all three bullets match the frontend word for word. Two lines do not. The link reads "…(opens in a new tab)" and goes to the animal-welfare-in-transport guidance, anchored at its section on transporting animals in connection with an economic activity — a different page, and one that lands the user on the specific section rather than at the top of a general one. The last sentence reads "Documents issued in any EU member state are not valid for use in GB.", in sentence case.

Bring the transporter authorisation guidance block into line with Design release 1: point the guidance link at https://www.gov.uk/guidance/animal-welfare-in-transport#transporting-animals-in-connection-with-an-economic-activity, change its text to end "(opens in a new tab)", and lower-case "member state" in the closing sentence. All three strings sit in the one guidance object at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:62-77, so this is a single edit to a single block rather than three scattered ones. Take the href from Design release 1 without the Google Analytics linker parameters its prototype copy carries — those are an artefact of how the URL was pasted, not part of the requirement. Where the block ends up on the page is settled by the flow change raised beside this one, which moves the guidance onto the transporter list; this finding is only about what it says.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the frontend's guidance link pointing at the animal-welfare-in-transport page, or Design release 1's pointing at transporting-animals-in-great-britain, in the two captured rendered DOMs.

increments.title: Frontend's transporter type question is headed "What type of transporter will move the animals?" and offers Commercial then Private, each explained; Design release 1 heads it "Choose a transporter type", warns the trader to search first, puts Private first and explains only Commercial
increments.detail:
The type question is headed "What type of transporter will move the animals?" as the page's h1 inside the fieldset legend, hinted "We will ask for the transporter's details next.", with no caption above it and no warning. It offers two radios in this order: Commercial, hinted "A business approved to transport animals — you will choose one from a list", then Private, hinted "You or another individual moving the animals — you will give their address". The copy is at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61 and the captured DOM of fe-transporter-type carries all of it verbatim. The page a trader reaches by answering Private is headed "Private transporter details" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:99), again with no caption.

Design release 1 heads the same question "Choose a transporter type" under a caption reading "Add a new transporter", and puts a warning between the heading and the radios: "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first." (app/views/transporter-add.html:31-36). The fieldset legend is visually hidden, so the heading does the work. The radios are the other way round — Private transporter first with no hint at all, then Commercial with one hint, "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." — and the labels differ too: "Private transporter" rather than "Private". The page reached by answering Private is headed "Add private transporter" under the same "Add a new transporter" caption (app/views/transporter-add-private.html:30-31).

Rewrite the type question's copy to match Design release 1 and rename the private form's heading with it. On the type page: change the heading to "Choose a transporter type", add the caption "Add a new transporter" above it, add a warning reading "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first.", drop the "We will ask for the transporter's details next." hint, reverse the two options so Private transporter comes first, relabel Private as "Private transporter", drop both of the frontend's explanatory hints and give Commercial the single hint "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." All of that is src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:60-61 and the template that reads it. On the private form: change the heading at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:99 from "Private transporter details" to "Add private transporter" and add the same "Add a new transporter" caption. This is copy on two pages Frontend already has and the band is frontend-work. increments.title: A Frontend user whose commercial transporter is not one of the two on the list has no way to record it; Design release 1 lets them add one, giving its authorisation number, name, address and contact details
increments.detail:
The commercial branch is select-only. The page is a radio group and nothing else: two transporters, a Save and continue button, a Save and return to hub button and a Cancel link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.njk:11-23). There is no add link, no add button and no add route — nothing in src/server matches a transporter add path — and the validator rejects any answer that is not one of the listed ids (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:22-28). The private branch is not an escape either: it collects a name, an address and contact details but no transporter authorisation number, so it cannot stand in for a commercial transporter. A user whose commercial transporter is not one of the two is left with no way to record it. They are not stopped — they can go back to the type question and declare the same firm as a private transporter, typing its name and address by hand — but the notification then carries the wrong transporter type and no approval number at all.

The transporter list carries an "Add a transporter" button under it (app/views/transporter.html:162-163). It leads to the type chooser, and choosing Commercial leads to a form headed "Add commercial transporter" under the caption "Add a new transporter". The form opens with a notification banner headed "Help with transporter authorisation" repeating the DAERA and APHA rules, then asks for: Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; Address line 1; Address line 2 (optional); Town or city; County (optional); Postcode or Zip code; Country, which is fixed to Northern Ireland and cannot be changed; then, under a sub-heading "Enter contact details", Email address and Phone number hinted "For international numbers include the country code". The type chooser states the same restriction in words: Commercial is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." The added transporter joins the list and can then be selected.

Add a page that lets a user enter a commercial transporter that is not on the list, reached from the transporter list rather than from the type question. It asks for a transporter authorisation number first, then name, the six address fields, a country locked to Northern Ireland, and an email address and phone number. The Northern Ireland restriction is a rule Design release 1 states twice and it has to be carried into the page and into the type chooser's hint. Design release 1 reads at first sight as though it contradicts itself on that restriction, and both parity runs checked it independently and reached the same answer, so nobody needs to chase it again: the rule is stated on the Commercial option's hint (app/data/transporter-types.js:6-10), enforced on the add form by a Country select rendered disabled over a hidden field carrying the real value (app/views/partials/transporter-add-commercial-fields.html:185-201), and reinforced by feeding that same form's address lookup only the Northern Ireland addresses (app/routes.js:3416-3420) — while Design release 1's own approved-transporter register holds four Commercial records, Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd of Dublin, Danish Meat Export ApS of Copenhagen and Portuguese Livestock Lda of Lisbon, and not one of them is in Northern Ireland. Every statement of the rule sits on the add route, so it governs a transporter a user creates by hand rather than the pre-approved register, which is why those four rows do not falsify it and why nothing follows for the frontend's own commercial list, whose Swiss and Belgian records are fixture data and not a finding. The frontend already stores a chosen commercial transporter as a name, an address and an approval number (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:75-81), so a hand-entered one fits the answer shape that already exists and no contract outside the frontend has to change. This depends on the transporter list gaining an add route, which is the flow change raised beside it.

increments.title: Frontend lists each transporter as a radio with one run-on line of address and approval number; Design release 1 lists them in a table that also shows each transporter's type and approval status
increments.detail:
Each transporter is one radio. Its label is the transporter's name and its hint is a single sentence built by joining the address lines with commas and appending the approval number after an em dash — "43 East Hague Extension, Delectus sitodio p. Laborum Odio tempor, Quasoccaecat ut ear, 30055, Switzerland — approval number ES-T2-45001294" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:92-93, built at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:55-65). Name, address and approval number are the only three facts shown, they are not aligned into columns, and nothing tells the user whether a transporter is approved. The underlying records carry nothing else to show: each holds an id, a name, an approval number and an address, and no type and no status (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29).

Each transporter is a table row under headed columns — Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status — with the selection radio in a leading column and a "View details" link in a trailing one (app/views/transporter.html:117-152). Type reads Commercial or Private. Status is a coloured tag: a green "Approved" on six of the eight rows and a pink "New" on Romanian Agri Exports SRL and Finnish Livestock Oy, which tells a user at a glance that a transporter has been added but not yet approved.

Render the transporter list as a table with a radio per row and columns for Name, Address, Approval number, Type and Status, and show the approval status as a tag. The type and the status are facts about a transporter that the frontend does not currently hold, so the local list at src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:7-29 has to gain both fields; that is a change inside the frontend's own fixture, not a new service, and Design release 1 hardcodes its own statuses the same way, so no API or contract has to land first. Filling the Status column is not mechanical, though: labelling the two records the frontend already ships as Approved would assert something nothing has verified, so whoever owns the commercial register has to say what each record may honestly be labelled before the column goes in, and when the register moves behind a service the status travels with it. Type only carries meaning once the list holds both commercial and private transporters, so schedule this after the flow change that combines them. Design release 1's "View details" link opens the transporter as an address-book record; whether the frontend has anywhere for that link to go is the address-book slice's question, not this one, so build the columns and leave the link out until that is settled.

increments.title: A private transporter added in DR1 joins the transporter list and can be picked again on the next notification; the frontend keeps it on the one notification it was typed into, so a repeat user retypes the same nine fields every time.
increments.detail:
`/transporters/private` collects the private transporter's name, five address lines, country, telephone number and email address and commits them onto the notification under `privateTransporter` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.controller.js). Nothing else reads them. The next notification starts the form blank, and there is nowhere in the service that lists transporters a user has entered before, so a haulier who moves the same animals every week retypes the same record every week.

Saving on DR1's add-private form pushes the transporter onto the user's own transporter records, and the `/transporter` list is built by concatenating those with the eight the service ships (app/routes.js:2903-2905, 3310-3345). The record the user just added is on the list the moment they return to it, alongside the approved ones, with its own Type and Status. Where the add was started from the address book, the same save also copies it into the address book.

Give a transporter somewhere to live other than the notification. That is a persistence change first — a per-organisation transporter collection, or an extension of the address book to carry a transporter's approval number, which the frontend's own note says the address book cannot represent today. Once records survive a notification, the list page shows them and the private form becomes an add-to-the-list step rather than a fill-in-the-blanks step. Ordered after the list page exists; useless before it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding the frontend writing the private transporter anywhere other than the notification's own answers — an address-book write, a per-organisation collection, or any read of previously entered transporters when the form loads.

finding.correction: CLAIMED: DR1 keeps an added private transporter on a reusable list, the frontend keeps it on the one notification, and persistence has to change first. VERIFIED ON BOTH SIDES. DR1 unshifts the new record onto sessionData.addedTransporters and builds the list page by concatenating those with the eight it ships (app/routes.js:3310-3316, 2903-2905), and copies it into the address book when the add was started from there. The frontend commits the fields onto the notification's own answers and nothing else reads them. BAND CONFIRMED FROM A REAL DEPENDENCY: the frontend has no per-organisation collection to write to and the notification is the only thing that persists, so a transporter register or an address-book extension has to exist before reuse means anything — the frontend's own commercial-transporter module records why the address book cannot stand in. MIS-CITED, slot left as it stands: evidence.frontend points at src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:1-6, which is that comment rather than the private form this finding is about; the primary frontend citation should be src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/private-transporter-details/private-transporter-details.controller.js. ONE THING TO KNOW BEFORE BUILDING: DR1's reuse is prototype session storage, not a database. It survives the notification but not the session, so DR1 shows the intent rather than the mechanism, and the shape of the store is the frontend's to decide. CONTROL FIXED: this finding named `privateTransporter`, which is the key the answers are committed under and not a thing anyone can point at on a page — no element on fe-transporter-private carries that name, so it resolved to nothing and no crop was taken. The page's own first field is `nameOrOrganisationName`, and that is what is named now; the nine boxes this finding says a repeat user retypes are `nameOrOrganisationName`, `addressLine1`, `addressLine2`, `townOrCity`, `county`, `postalOrZipCode`, `country`, `telephoneNumber` and `emailAddress`, and a crop of the first of them frames the form the finding is about. The frontend slot still says `privateTransporter` and should, because that is the correct name for where the answers land.
