increments.title: Two ports appear twice in the frontend's port-of-entry list under different codes — Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness — so a user picking one has to guess which of two identically named entries is the right one; DR1's list names each port once.
increments.detail:
The port-of-entry search offers seventy-eight ports, and two of them are listed twice. Pembroke Port appears under GB PED and again under GB PEM; Port of Sheerness appears under GBSHS and again under GB SHS, the second of the pair differing only by a space in the code (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:182-189, 254-261). Typing "Pembroke" returns two results with identical text, and the user has no way to tell which one the service expects — the codes are the only thing that separates them and nothing on the page explains what a code means. Whichever they pick is stored, so the same physical port arrives at the backend under two different codes depending on which line the user happened to click.

DR1's catalogue names Sheerness once, under GBSHS (app/data/uk-airports.js:175), and has no Pembroke entry at all. It is not free of repeated names, though: eight places appear twice under different codes — Aberdeen, Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester and Southampton — the airport and the seaport sharing one name. DR1 prints the code after the name, so a user choosing Aberdeen picks between "Aberdeen - ABZ" and "Aberdeen - GBABD" with nothing else to separate them.

Nothing to build until it is settled whether one name under two codes is a defect at all, because DR1 does the same thing eight times over and both services print the code beside the name. What would settle it: the reference-data owner saying whether GB PED and GB PEM are two facilities or one record duplicated. The other pair is worth raising whatever the answer — GBSHS and "GB SHS" are the same five characters with a space gained or lost, which is a data defect on its own terms — but it belongs in a reference-data ticket rather than in this backlog, because DR1 gives no position to compare it against.

FALSIFIED BY: DR1's own port catalogue carrying two entries that share a name and differ only by code. Already observed, on eight names, which is why this finding is disputed rather than accepted.

Typing "Pembroke" returns two results with identical text, and the user has no way to tell which one the service expects — the codes are the only thing that separates them and nothing on the page explains what a code means. Whichever they pick is stored, so the same physical port arrives at the backend under two different codes depending on which line the user happened to click.
finding.prototype: DR1's catalogue names Sheerness once, under GBSHS (app/data/uk-airports.js:175), and has no Pembroke entry at all. It is not free of repeated names, though: eight places appear twice under different codes — Aberdeen, Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester and Southampton — the airport and the seaport sharing one name. DR1 prints the code after the name, so a user choosing Aberdeen picks between "Aberdeen - ABZ" and "Aberdeen - GBABD" with nothing else to separate them.
finding.difference: Nothing to build until it is settled whether one name under two codes is a defect at all, because DR1 does the same thing eight times over and both services print the code beside the name. What would settle it: the reference-data owner saying whether GB PED and GB PEM are two facilities or one record duplicated. The other pair is worth raising whatever the answer — GBSHS and "GB SHS" are the same five characters with a space gained or lost, which is a data defect on its own terms — but it belongs in a reference-data ticket rather than in this backlog, because DR1 gives no position to compare it against.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: the frontend lists Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness twice while DR1 names every port once. FRONTEND LEG TRUE: the fixture holds GB PED and GB PEM both named 'Pembroke Port' and GBSHS and 'GB SHS' both named 'Port of Sheerness' (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:182-189, 253-260), and the captured DOM renders 'Pembroke Port (GB PED)' beside 'Pembroke Port (GB PEM)'. PROTOTYPE LEG FALSE: DR1's catalogue repeats eight names under different codes — Aberdeen (ABZ and GBABD), Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester (MAN and GBMNC) and Southampton (SOU and GBSOU) — because it lists the airport and the seaport separately. The captured dr1-arrival-details DOM renders 'Aberdeen - ABZ' and 'Aberdeen - GBABD'. DR1 is the oracle and DR1 behaves the same way, so the parity claim does not stand. ALSO OVERSTATED: 'two results with identical text'. Both services append the code, so the option text is not identical — the finding's own next clause concedes the codes separate them. And DR1 has no Pembroke entry of any kind, so it takes no position on that pair. HOW CHECKED: uniq -d over the name and code literals in app/data/uk-airports.js; grep of the rendered option text in capture/html/frontend/fe-arrival-details.html and capture/html/prototype/dr1-arrival-details.html. BAND: needs-backend to disputed.
finding.falsifiedBy: DR1's own port catalogue carrying two entries that share a name and differ only by code. Already observed, on eight names, which is why this finding is disputed rather than accepted.

relatedTo.why: Both are defects in the same reference-data port catalogue and would be fixed in one pass

provenance.note: C raised nothing about port-catalogue contents. C's only port finding (inc-069, import-reason) opens by declaring itself "a design decision rather than fixture contents", which reads as a deliberate scope choice to leave fixture data quality out of the run. So this is a C miss by policy rather than by oversight. A itself bands it disputed, because DR1 repeats a name under two codes eight times over — so it is a weak finding either way, and the honest half of it (GBSHS vs "GB SHS", the same code with a stray space) A already says belongs in a reference-data ticket, not this backlog.

increments.title: Three port names are malformed in the frontend's port-of-entry list — a misspelt Teesport, a shouted TILBURY and a Portsmouth Port with a doubled space — where DR1 spells every port in ordinary sentence case.
increments.detail:
Three of the seventy-eight ports a user can pick are written wrong. GB TEE is named "Teestort", which is not a place — Teesport is (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:302-305). GB TIL is named "TILBURY" in capitals, sitting on the same list as "Tilbury Port" and "Tilbury 2 Ro-Ro Terminal" in ordinary case (:294-297). GB PME is named "Portsmouth  Port" with two spaces between the words (:266-269). The misspelling is the one that costs a user something: the search matches on the text as written, so typing "Teesport" returns nothing and the port looks absent from the service.

DR1's catalogue spells two of the same places properly and in ordinary case — Teesport (app/data/uk-airports.js:186) and Tilbury (:189). It has no Portsmouth entry at all, so DR1 takes no position on that third name.

Correct the three names in the reference-data port catalogue: Teestort to Teesport, TILBURY to title case, and the doubled space in Portsmouth Port to one. The codes do not change, so nothing already submitted is affected. The list reaches the frontend from the reference-data service and is only captured into the repo as a fixture, so the correction lands upstream and the fixture is recaptured after it.

increments.title: DR1 offers only the trader's own GB branch addresses as the consignment contact; the frontend offers the whole address book, overseas consignors included.
increments.detail:
The contact page offers `addressBook.all(orgId)` — every record in the organisation's book, in book order (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:69-74). fe-contact shows thirteen radios, the same thirteen records the party pickers page through, and they include Astra Rosales in Switzerland, Danish Meat Export ApS in Denmark, Laiterie du Nord SARL in France and Iberian Swine SA in Spain. So a trader can name a Spanish exporter as the person responsible for the consignment once it is inside Great Britain, and nothing on the page discourages it. The address book holds no type by which the list could be narrowed — the service says so in its own contract, "Addresses have no type in the address book (D3) — the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15).

DR1 draws this list from a separate collection of branch addresses, not from the consignment address book the pickers use (app/data/contact-addresses.js:1-21, rendered at app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:68-83). dr1-contact-address-for-consignment shows three, all in Great Britain: Aberdeen Livestock Ltd in Aberdeen, West Country Livestock Ltd in Bristol, Cymru Animal Imports Ltd in Cardiff. The page says what the list is for — the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain — and the help line names the collection when it tells the trader where a missing one comes from: "add a new branch address" (:65). That collection is one of DR1's own address types: saving an address in the book begins by asking "What is the new address for?" over Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and, after a divider, Branch Address (app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38), and the contact list is the Branch Address type and nothing else.

Narrow the contact list to the trader's own branch addresses. That needs the address book to distinguish a branch record from a party record — DR1's Branch Address type — which today it deliberately does not, so the API and the record shape have to change before the page can. Until then the page offers a choice DR1 rules out, and the frontend's own hint does not warn against it. The narrower question of what the page says the contact is for is a separate copy change on the same page.

FALSIFIED BY: A DR1 contact list drawn from the same address collection as the consignment pickers, or an address-book record carrying a type or category the frontend could filter on today.

The frontend page renders thirteen radios, and the four overseas records the finding names are all there — Astra Rosales in Bern, Danish Meat Export ApS in Copenhagen, Laiterie du Nord SARL in Lille and Iberian Swine SA in Huesca. increments.title: Frontend offers the trader's entire address book on all six address pickers; Design release 1 offers only the addresses saved for that role, and only branch addresses for the contact
increments.detail:
All five party pickers and the contact-address page draw from one undifferentiated list. Every captured picker reports "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" and every one of them offers the same thirteen records in the same order, whether the trader is choosing a place of origin abroad or a consignee in Great Britain — the place-of-origin picker and the consignee picker both lead with Astra Rosales in Switzerland, Tech Imports Ltd in London and Origin Farm in Ireland. Those two pickers are byte-identical in the captured DOM — same caption, same five rows in the same order, the remaining eight behind the same pagination — so the page that asks for the farm the animals left offers Great Britain importers, and the page that asks who is receiving them offers foreign farms. A Danish meat exporter is offered as the place of origin, as the consignee and as the importer alike, and nothing on any of those three pages objects. The contact-address page lists the same book again, all thirteen as radios (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/controller.js:69-75, which calls `addressBook.all`). This is deliberate: the address-book service states that addresses have no type, because the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next, and so no function it exposes takes a role (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15). The picker controller calls the book with a query and a page number and nothing else (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:36), so no amount of real data changes what these pages offer: there is no field to filter on. The consequence for the trader is that every picker asks them to find the right kind of address in a list that is mostly the wrong kind, with nothing on the page marking which is which.

Design release 1 types every saved address and filters each picker to its type. Place of origin offers nine foreign farms, consignor nine, consignee six Great Britain importers, importer six, place of destination three — different lists, from the same book, with the section's own type deciding what appears (app/routes.js:3457-3466 and app/routes.js:3520-3543). The types are the trader's own: saving an address begins by asking "What is the new address for?" over Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and, after a divider, Branch Address (app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38). The contact address is the Branch Address type, held as its own list of the organisation's branches (app/data/contact-addresses.js:1-21), which is why Design release 1's contact page says "add a new branch address" rather than "add an address".

Give a saved address one or more roles and filter each picker by the role it is asking for, including the contact page, which asks only for a branch address. The frontend cannot do this alone: its address-book service reads a book that carries no type at all and exposes no role-aware call (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-19), so the address-book API — the Standard Address Block records in trade-imports-address-book — has to carry the type first, and whichever service writes those records has to collect it. Decide it together with the address-book scope question raised as address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, because the type is collected on the add form that question is about. This is a live defect in the notification journey whichever way that scope question is settled: it is about what the pickers Frontend already has show today, not about pages Frontend does not have, so it survives a ruling that the eight address-book screens belong to another service. Until the type exists, no useful half of this can ship: filtering on a guess, such as matching the country against the direction of travel, would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants. `controls` is deliberately empty: what differs is which rows are in the table, so the whole table on each of two pickers is the shot, and the only named control on those rows, `party`, occurs once per row and would be refused a crop.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding two frontend pickers whose captured lists differ. All five report "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" and the first five rows of fe-address-picker-place-of-origin, fe-address-picker-consignee, fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter, fe-address-picker-importer and fe-address-picker-place-of-destination are identical.

increments.title: A Frontend user whose address is not already saved reaches a dead end on every address-selection page; Design release 1 offers a route to add a new address on all of them and returns the user with the new address chosen
increments.detail:
On any of Frontend's five consignment party pickers, a search that matches nothing renders one line — "No addresses match your search." — and nothing else: no link, no button, no guidance (fe-address-picker-place-of-origin-no-matches). The only control left is "Save and continue", and submitting without a row selected returns "Select a consignor from the list" in an error summary (fe-address-picker-consignor-or-exporter-error), so the page cannot be satisfied at all. The picker form is a search input, a Search button, the results table, its pagination and Save and continue, and nothing more (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-113); the addresses feature's copy holds no add-an-address key at all, the empty state's only string being noMatches (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:43-62). The contact-address page is a different shape — the whole book as thirteen radios rather than a search — but it is the same dead end: it offers no way to add an address either (fe-contact). Searching the rendered DOM of every one of the 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "add a new address", "add an address" or "address book" returns nothing. So a trader whose place of origin has never been saved cannot finish the addresses section, and the service gives them no way to find that out except by failing.

Design release 1 gives every address-selection page a route out to add one. On the five party pickers it is a secondary "Add a new address" button sitting under the results table and above "Save and continue" — six captured screens carry it, the five picker headings plus the search-filtered state — pointing at /address-book/add?from=<section> (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:162-163, with the href built at app/routes.js:3598-3600). On the contact-address page it is worded differently and sits above the radios, as a link inside the sentence "If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.", pointing at /address-book/add?from=contact-address. Following either skips the address-type chooser, because the section the user came from implies the type and is carried in a hidden addressType, and lands on "Add address details" (dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker), where the address can be searched for or typed in by hand. Saving writes the address to the book, selects it into the section the user came from, redirects them back to that same page and shows a success message naming the address just added (app/routes.js:8118-8194). The notification is never abandoned.

Give every address-selection page a route out, and a return path back to it with the new address selected — the five pickers and the contact-address page. Nothing has to land first: the address-book API behind Frontend already serves create, and every other part of the picker exists. The two runs disagree about what that means for the band: run C banded this frontend-work on exactly that ground, where run A banded it needs-backend, on the ground that this service's address-book client is read-only by decision and creating a record belongs to the Import Notification Service front door. What turns on the answer is only where the add page lives, not whether the trader is given a route out of the dead end, and the API already serving create is the harder fact, so the band taken here is frontend-work. Run A also carries something this run does not: the workspace has already accepted the missing route as a deliberate temporary measure, with traders who need a new address hopping across to the address book by themselves. So this is a gap against Design release 1 that is real and currently accepted, rather than the next thing to fix. What a person has to choose is the destination, and it is the same choice this run's scope question turns on (address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent) — either an add-address page inside this frontend, which means giving its address-book service a write path it deliberately does not have (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19), or a link out to the Import Notification Service front door's existing /address-book/add, which needs a return URL so the user comes back to the page they left rather than being stranded in another service's address book. The empty state's copy is part of the work either way: "No addresses match your search." is a statement with no next step in it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any link or button on a Frontend party picker or the contact-address page that leads to adding an address.

increments.title: Frontend gives the list of addresses no heading and captions it "Showing 5 of 13 addresses"; Design release 1 heads it "Select an address" and counts "Showing 9 out of 9 results"
increments.detail:
On a party picker the results table has no heading above it — the table's own caption carries the count, "Showing 5 of 13 addresses", and the trader goes straight from the Search button to a table (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:51-53, wording at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:51). On the contact-address page there is no heading and no count at all: the radios sit directly under the page heading and its hint. So neither page tells the trader in words that the thing below is a list to choose one item from.

Design release 1 heads the list "Select an address" on both surfaces — as an h2 above the results with the count beneath it on a party picker (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:94-96), and as an h2 above the radios on the contact-address page (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:62). The count reads "Showing 9 out of 9 results", naming both the number shown and the number there are, and it updates as the trader filters.

Head the list of addresses "Select an address" on the five party pickers and on the contact-address page, and reword the count as "Showing {shown} out of {total} results". The count wording is one function in the addresses copy (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:51) plus its Welsh counterpart; the heading is a new line in each of the two templates. On the picker, sequence this after the pagination change raised as addresses--picker-pages-results-and-searches-on-the-server, because the numbers the count reports change with it. `controls` is deliberately empty: the finding is about a heading and a caption, neither of which is a control the crop can resolve, and the whole-page shot is what shows both.

increments.title: Frontend's contact-address page explains what selecting does; Design release 1 explains who the contact is and what they are responsible for
increments.detail:
Under the heading "Contact address for consignment" the page's only guidance is the fieldset hint "Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/template.njk:11-23). That sentence describes what the service does with the answer. It does not say who the contact is, what they are responsible for, or over what period — so a trader choosing between the addresses in front of them is given no basis for the choice.

Design release 1 puts a paragraph directly under the heading: "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:50-52). It defines the role and its window, and it is the same sentence Design release 1 uses to describe the Branch Address type when a trader saves one. Design release 1 says nothing anywhere about copying the name and address into the notification.

Replace the hint with Design release 1's sentence, as a paragraph under the heading rather than as a fieldset hint, so it reads as guidance about the question and not as a note about the control. One string in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4 and its Welsh counterpart, and a move from the radios' `hint` slot to body copy in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/template.njk:11-23. What the frontend's current sentence records — that this party is stored as a copy rather than a reference, unlike consignor, consignee, importer and destination (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:61-70) — is a fact about storage that Design release 1 does not put in front of the trader, and dropping it from the page loses nothing the trader can act on.

increments.title: Check your answers drops the whole Documents section when nothing has been uploaded, so a trader with no documents has no route to the upload page from the review; Design release 1 always shows the section with a Change link
increments.detail:
The captured Check your answers page ends at "3. Addresses" and has no Documents heading, no Uploaded documents card and no link to the upload page. That is not an accident of the capture: the documents card returns nothing when the collection is empty (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/cards/documents.js:35-37) and the section that would hold it is then dropped from the page altogether (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/sections/documents.js:9-12, and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/index.js:16-21 appends it only when it exists). Documents are optional for submission, so this is the ordinary case rather than an edge one: a trader who has uploaded nothing sees no mention of documents on the page they are told to check before submitting, and has to go back to the task list to find the upload page.

Design release 1 gives documents a permanent numbered section of its own, "4. Documents", with the subsection heading "Upload documents" and an "Uploaded documents" card carrying a Change link to /upload-documents (app/views/review-notification.html:160-165). The section is not conditional. With nothing uploaded the card still stands, empty, under its heading and with its Change link — so the review page always states that documents are part of the notification and always offers the route to add them.

Render the Documents section unconditionally on Check your answers, with the Uploaded documents card and its Change link present even when the collection is empty. That means removing the two early returns that suppress it and giving the empty card a state to render. The change is contained to the check-answers view-model and template — no new answers and no obligation change — and the upload page it links to already exists. It should land with the section-spine rework, which is what puts Documents at position 4.

increments.title: Frontend will not accept a notification until every animal has been identified; Design release 1 accepts one with no identifiers at all and asks for them after submission
increments.detail:
A trader cannot submit until every animal on every commodity line has an identifier record. The animal-identifier group carries a count rule as well as a content rule: each unit record must hold at least one of the six identifiers, and the number of unit records on a commodity line must equal the number of animals declared for that line (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:98-101, `recordCountEquals` against `numberOfAnimals`). That group is the whole of the `animalIdentification` task row (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45), and readiness demands every task row be fulfilled, not applicable or optional (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15). Readiness is the gate on both the review section (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:81-85) and the submit itself, which returns `ok: false` and goes nowhere without it (src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9-15). So a trader who declares twenty animals must fill in twenty identifier cards before the service will take the notification, and a trader bringing in two hundred salmon must enter two hundred records before the service will show them their own notification. Documents are the one thing Frontend does let through: the documents group carries no minimum, so an empty collection is not a bar.

Design release 1 asks for none of it on a single-species consignment. Its submit gate ends with the line "Documents remain optional. Animal identifiers are optional unless multiple species are selected, in which case at least one identifier is required per species" (app/routes.js:4562-4566). The two predicates behind that line are `requiresAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit`, which is true only when the consignment holds more than one species and at least one of them has an identifier set, and `hasMinimumAnimalIdentifiersForSubmit`, which returns true outright when the first is false: so the minimum passes for a single-species consignment however many identifier fields that commodity carries, and for a multi-species one it asks for a single complete entry per species, never one per animal (app/routes.js:1511-1523). The captured review page is the proof: a notification of five Bison bison with no identifier saved shows an empty "Bison Bison" card under "Identification details", no error summary, and a live Continue button. Design release 1 then chases what is missing rather than refusing it — the submitted page carries "You still need to:" with "complete the animal identifier information in the notification" as a bullet.

Move the animal-identifier requirement out of the submit gate and into the follow-up. Concretely: keep the per-record rule that a saved animal must carry at least one identifier, but stop the `animalIdentification` task row blocking readiness — drop `recordCountEquals` from the unit-record obligation's `requires` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:98-101) so an under-identified line no longer holds the row out of FULFILLED. Dropping the count rule on its own would leave identifiers wholly optional, and that is not Design release 1's rule: what replaces the count is the multi-species condition, so that identifiers are required for submission only where more than one commodity line carries a typed identifier set, and then only one complete record per line rather than one per animal. The count itself is still worth showing on the hub and on Check your answers as progress; it just must not stop a submission. Then say what is outstanding after submission, which is the work in review--no-outstanding-tasks-after-submitting; that finding parks its identifier bullet because the frontend cannot currently reach the confirmation page with animals unidentified, and this change is what unparks it. Nothing has to land first: the obligation, the task row and the readiness roll-up are all frontend files, and the animals backend's submit transition rejects a notification only on its status, never on its content, so no contract or API change is needed to accept a partly identified one.

The captured dr1-review-notification-incomplete lists exactly four problems — "Complete arrival details", "Complete transport details", "Complete roles and addresses", "Complete contact address for this consignment" — and no identifier among them, on a notification that had saved none.

relatedTo.why: That finding adds the outstanding-work section to the confirmation page but parks its identifier bullet because the frontend cannot reach that page with animals unidentified; this finding is what makes the bullet reachable, so the two are one change in two halves.

increments.title: Check your answers gives no sign that a notification is incomplete; Design release 1 heads the review page with "There is a problem", names each unfinished section and refuses to go on
increments.detail:
A trader who reaches Check your answers before the notification is finished sees a page that looks finished. Every unanswered row reads "Not provided" in ordinary black text, no card is marked, there is no error summary, and the page still ends with the heading "Now submit your notification", the sentence "Continue to the declaration to submit your notification." and a green Continue button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114). Nothing on the page says what is outstanding or where to go to finish it. Pressing Continue is not refused either: the POST handler redirects straight on to the declaration (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/controller.js:96-99), the declaration renders, and only after the trader ticks the box and presses Continue again does the submit fail its readiness check and bounce back to Check your answers with no message at all (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/controller.js:86-88, src/server/app/engine/write/submit.js:9-15). The trader ends up back where they started having been told nothing.

Design release 1's review page opens with a red-bordered "There is a problem" summary carrying one link per unfinished card — "Complete arrival details", "Complete transport details", "Complete roles and addresses", "Complete contact address for this consignment" — each anchored to the card it names (app/views/review-notification.html:29-36, the list built from the unfinished cards at app/routes.js:4520-4527). The number of entries follows how far the notification got: a notification answered only as far as the reason for import carries five, adding "Complete additional details". Every unfinished card is drawn with a red left bar and repeats its own message in red inside the card, above its own rows (app/routes.js:4473-4482), and each of its rows keeps its label and loses its value rather than being filled with a placeholder — the empty value is marked missing to a screen reader (app/routes.js:4134-4165) — so the page reads as a list of what is left rather than a wall of filler text. The cards that are answered look exactly as they do on a complete notification, with their Change link and their values. Continue does not move on: the POST re-renders the same page with the same summary until the notification is complete (app/routes.js:10068-10075).

Give Check your answers the incomplete state Design release 1 shows. On render, work out which cards are unfinished and put an error summary above the heading listing one "Complete <card name>" link per unfinished card, anchored to that card; mark each unfinished card with its own inline error message; blank the unanswered values rather than filling them; and make the POST re-render the page rather than continue to the declaration when the notification is not ready. The readiness signal already exists — `scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers` — and the per-card breakdown can come from the same task-row statuses the hub uses (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js). Nothing has to land first. `controls` is deliberately empty: the finding is the state of the whole page, not one field, and a crop of any single row would hide the error summary that is the substance of it.

increments.title: Check your answers puts a Change link on every row, so a finished notification offers twenty-four of them; Design release 1 puts one Change link in each card's heading and none on the rows
increments.detail:
Every row of every card carries its own Change link on the right-hand side, with visually hidden text naming the row and its card — "Change country of origin (Import details)", "Change transporter approval number (Transport details)" and so on. A finished notification shows twenty-four of them — twenty-two on rows, plus two in the heading of the Species card, which is the only card on the page with card-level actions. An unfinished notification shows eighteen, all on rows; the exact count tracks how many answers the notification carries rather than anything about the page's shape. Each link goes to the page that collects that one answer, with a `change=1` flag so the trader is returned to the review afterwards (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/summary-row.js:14-21, building the action at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/change-link.js:12-25 and rendering it through govukSummaryList at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:96-102). So the page repeats the same destination link once per row: five rows in the Arrival details card all lead to the arrival details page, five in Roles and addresses all lead to the roles and addresses page.

Design release 1 puts one Change link in each card's heading bar, level with the card title, and no link on any row (app/views/partials/review-summary-card.html:23-28 renders the single title link from the card's own changeHref, and app/views/partials/review-summary-row.html:14-24 renders a row as a key and a value with no action at all). Both the finished and the unfinished review page carry exactly eleven Change links, one per card, each going to the page that collects that card's answers. Eleven is the count for these captures rather than a fixed number: Design release 1's Transit countries card is conditional (app/views/review-notification.html:151-153) and absent from both, so a notification that named transit countries would show twelve — one per card still.

Move the Change link from the row to the card. Give each card in the check-answers view-model one action, pointing at the page that collects that card's answers, and stop attaching a change action to individual rows — that is `summary-row.js` dropping its call to `changeAction`, and each card builder gaining the card-level action the Species card already has, with the Species card itself collapsing from two heading links to one. The visually hidden text moves with it, from naming the row to naming the card. Nothing has to land first, and the destinations do not change: every row in a card already resolves to the same page, so no route is lost. `controls` is deliberately empty for two reasons: the finding is the arrangement of the whole page rather than any one field, and "Change" lands twenty-four times on the frontend page, so naming it would get the crop refused and fall back to the whole-page shot anyway.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a Change link on a row of any card in the captured dr1-review-notification, or a card whose rows carry no Change link in the captured fe-check-answers. Design release 1's row macro has no action branch at all, and the frontend's row builder attaches one to every row it makes.

increments.title: The read-only view of an already-submitted notification still ends with "Now submit your notification" and a Continue button; Design release 1 renders no form once a notification is submitted
increments.detail:
When a notification has been submitted and the trader opens it through the View link on the dashboard, the review page is redrawn read-only: the status tag turns green and reads "Submitted", every Change link is removed, and "Copy as new" and "Delete" buttons appear at the top. The flag doing that is set from the journey status (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/controller.js:81). But the foot of the page is unchanged. It still carries the heading "Now submit your notification", the sentence "Continue to the declaration to submit your notification." and a green Continue button (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114, which is outside every read-only branch on the page). So a page that has just told the trader the notification is submitted, and that has removed every other way of changing it, invites them to submit it again — and pressing Continue goes to the declaration, which redirects a submitted journey straight to the confirmation page (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/controller.js:49-54), so the trader lands on a confirmation for a notification they did not just submit.

Design release 1 wraps the whole form in a read-only test and renders nothing at the foot of the page for a submitted notification (app/views/review-notification.html:180-186). The read-only review ends with the last card, presenting a submitted notification as a record with no action on it. This half is read from the view rather than from a picture: Design release 1 captured no submitted review, so the prototype screen in this pair is its draft review. The state that would show it is a Design release 1 review page reached with a `submitted` query parameter, which is the only way that side renders read-only (app/routes.js:10026-10037).

Suppress the submit block — heading, sentence and Continue button — when the review is read-only. The template already receives a `readOnly` flag and uses it for the Change links and the Copy and Delete buttons, so this is one condition around the closing block in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/template.njk:108-114 and nothing new has to be worked out.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding no Continue button on fe-check-answers-submitted. The captured DOM carries the heading "Now submit your notification" and a submitting form with a Continue button, on a page whose status strip reads "Submitted".

increments.title: Check your answers groups the notification into three numbered sections; Design release 1 uses six that mirror the task list, with a heading above every card
increments.detail:
The page has three numbered sections — "1. About the consignment", "2. Movement", "3. Addresses" — plus a "4. Documents" that only appears when a document has been uploaded (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:35-40), the four of them assembled in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/index.js:6-22. Section 1 carries three subheadings, "Consignment details", "Commodity details" and "Species" (named at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:41-45 and attached at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/sections/about-consignment.js:20-34); sections 2 and 3 carry none at all, passing a null group heading (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/sections/movement.js:12-19, src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/sections/addresses.js:16-25), so their cards sit directly under the numbered heading. The grouping does not follow the task list either: commodity and animal details sit under "About the consignment" rather than in a section about the goods, roles and the contact address share one "Addresses" section, and the countries a consignment travels through is a row inside the Arrival details card rather than a heading of its own.

Design release 1 has six numbered sections — "1. About the consignment", "2. Description of the goods", "3. Transport and arrival", "4. Documents", "5. Consignment parties", "6. Contact address" — and a subsection heading above every single card (app/views/review-notification.html:41-179). Those subheadings run, in order, "Where is this consignment coming from?", "What are you importing?", "Main reason for import", "Commodity details", "Identification details", "Additional details", "Arrival details", "Transit countries", "Transport details", "Upload documents", "Roles and addresses" and "Contact address for this consignment" — three of them phrased as the questions the trader answered rather than as the name of a card. Transit countries gets its own subheading and card when it applies (app/views/review-notification.html:150-153), the reason for import gets its own card rather than sitting among animal details, and the contact address is lifted out of the parties section into a numbered section of its own.

Restructure the page into Design release 1's six sections in its order, and give every card a subsection heading. That means splitting the current "1. About the consignment" into "1. About the consignment" and "2. Description of the goods"; renaming "2. Movement" to "3. Transport and arrival" and lifting transit countries out of the Arrival details card into its own headed card; keeping Documents at 4 and moving it ahead of the parties; splitting "3. Addresses" into "5. Consignment parties" and "6. Contact address"; and moving the reason for import out of the Additional animal details card into its own card under "Main reason for import". The work is in the four section builders under src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/sections/ and the copy file beside them; the template already renders a heading per group. This is copy and view-model restructuring only — no new answers are collected, so nothing blocks it — and doing it at the same time as the hub's own section spine keeps the two pages agreeing with each other. `controls` is deliberately empty: the finding is the arrangement of the whole page and a crop of any one heading would not show it.

increments.title: Check your answers prints "Not provided" both for a question that does not apply and for an answer that is still needed; Design release 1 says "Not applicable" for the first and marks the second as missing
increments.detail:
One string stands in for every empty value. On the complete notification, "Region of origin code", "Internal reference number" and "Number of packages" all read "Not provided" — and they are questions that genuinely do not apply, because the trader answered No to the region-code question and the internal reference is optional. On the unfinished notification, "Port of entry" also reads "Not provided" — and that one is required before the notification can be submitted. The two states are typeset identically, so a trader reading the page cannot tell which rows are finished business and which are work still to do. The single string comes from `notProvided` in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:3, applied to every blank value at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/view-model/rows/value-text.js:11-13.

Design release 1 has two different treatments. A value that does not apply is written out as "Not applicable" (app/routes.js:4065-4071) — that is what its review page shows against "Region of origin code" and "Internal reference number". A value that is required and absent is not given text at all: the row is drawn in the missing style with only a visually hidden "Missing" for a screen reader (app/views/partials/review-summary-row.html:15-21), inside a card that is itself marked with an error. The two treatments interlock rather than compete — the emptiness test at app/routes.js:4073-4077 counts the literal string "Not applicable" as empty, which is how a row that already carries the placeholder gets blanked once its card goes into error. So on Design release 1 the eye can separate "nothing needed here" from "something still owed here" without reading a word.

Split the one placeholder into two, and follow Design release 1 in deciding per card rather than per row. In a card that is complete, print "Not applicable" for every empty value — one string in the English check-answers copy file and one in the Welsh. In a card that is unfinished — the same cards that would carry the inline error from review--incomplete-notification-not-flagged-on-check-answers — print no placeholder text at all: draw every empty row in a missing style with only a visually hidden "Missing", whether that particular row was required or optional. The frontend already knows which cards are unfinished, because the same task-row statuses drive the hub, so this is a rendering change in the check-answers view-model with nothing to land first.

increments.title: The review page calls the arrival date "Arrival date at port of entry" where Design release 1 calls it "Arrival date at destination" — but Design release 1's own question page calls it "at port of entry", so the two releases of that label disagree inside Design release 1
increments.detail:
The Arrival details card on Check your answers labels the row "Arrival date at port of entry" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/check-answers/copy/copy.en.js:70), the same words the question page uses when it asks for the answer (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:5) and the same words the validation message repeats when the date is missing (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:35). Question, summary and error message all agree.

Design release 1 labels the same value two different ways on two of its own screens. Its arrival-details question asks for "Arrival date at port of entry" (app/views/partials/arrival-date-picker.html:9), storing the answer as `arrivalDateAtPort`; its review page then prints that same stored value under the key "Arrival date at destination" (app/routes.js:4676-4679), and its dashboard cards use "Arrival date at destination" too. A port of entry and a place of destination are two different places in this service — the notification collects an address for each — so the two labels do not describe the same thing, and only one of them can be right.

Nothing should change until somebody says which label Design release 1 means. This is banded disputed because Design release 1 contradicts itself between two of its own screens rather than because the frontend might be wrong. The observation that settles it is a ruling on whether the date being collected is the arrival at the port of entry or the arrival at the place of destination. If it is the port of entry, Design release 1's review and dashboard labels are the mistake and the frontend is already right. If it is the destination, then both sides' question pages are mislabelled as well as the frontend's review row, and on the frontend that is three strings rather than one — the review row, the question page label and the validation message that quotes it — so the change is much wider than the single row it looks like.

increments.title: The declaration states three bare headings where Design release 1 states each one and then explains what it commits the trader to
increments.detail:
The page is three headings, a four-item list and two closing sentences, with no supporting text under any heading (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js:3-18). The first heading, "I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK.", stands alone. The second is a single long heading, "I confirm I am responsible for this consignment until it has cleared border control checks or reached the place of destination." The accountability list reads "payments for border control checks", "re-dispatch of the consignment", "quarantine or isolation of the animals", "the costs of destruction and disposal". So a trader ticking the box is agreeing to four compressed phrases with no statement of when the responsibility starts or which regulation it sits under.

Design release 1 gives each statement a heading and a body (app/views/declaration.html:40-64). "I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK." is followed by "I am complying with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 including on animal health and welfare." "I confirm I am responsible for this consignment." is followed by "I am responsible from the submission of this notification to when it enters Great Britain. And I am responsible until it has either:" and two bullets, "cleared official checks at the border" and "reached the Place of Destination as stated on the health certificate or notification". The accountability list reads "any payment for the official controls at the border", "any arrangements to re-dispatch the consignment", "any costs needed for quarantine or isolation of consignments", "any costs needed for destruction and disposal of consignments, when instructed by the authorities". The two closing sentences are the same on both sides, and so is the checkbox label.

Replace the declaration body copy with Design release 1's wording, in English and Welsh: add the Regulation (EU) 2017/625 sentence under the first heading; shorten the second heading to "I confirm I am responsible for this consignment." and add the sentence and two bullets beneath it; and reword the four accountability items. This is a legal statement the trader is asked to affirm, so it has to be taken whole rather than approximated — as it stands the frontend commits the trader to less than Design release 1 asks for, and says nothing about when responsibility begins. The work is a copy change in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/declaration/copy/copy.en.js and its Welsh counterpart, plus the small template change needed to render a paragraph and a nested list under the first two headings. `controls` is deliberately empty: the finding is the body of the declaration, which is prose rather than any one control, and the checkbox beneath it is word-for-word identical on both sides.

increments.title: After submitting, the frontend never tells the trader what is still outstanding; Design release 1 heads the submitted page with "Before the consignment is imported" and lists the documents and identifiers still owed
increments.detail:
The confirmation page goes straight from the green panel to "Transporting the consignment" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/confirmation/template.njk:4-13). There is no section about work still to do, and nothing in the confirmation copy or controller that could produce one. This matters because the frontend does accept a submission with no documents at all: the documents group carries neither a minimum entry count nor a required-one-of rule (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/documents.js:19-27), so an untouched documents collection rolls up as optional and the readiness check passes without it. A trader can therefore submit a notification with no health certificate attached, reach a page headed "Import notification submitted", and be told nothing about the certificate.

Design release 1 puts a section between the panel and the transport guidance whenever anything is still outstanding: "Before the consignment is imported", the line "You still need to:", and a bulleted list (app/views/notification-submitted.html:27-36). The list is built at submission time and holds only the two things Design release 1 lets a trader submit without: "upload the health certificate and any other required documents", shown whenever no document has been uploaded, and "complete the animal identifier information in the notification", shown when identifiers were allowed through the submit gate — a soft follow-up once the per-species minimum is met — but are not yet complete (app/routes.js:5674-5692). Everything else Design release 1 treats as mandatory and refuses to submit without, so the section never carries it, and the section disappears entirely when nothing is outstanding.

Add the same section to the confirmation page: a heading "Before the consignment is imported", the line "You still need to:", and one bullet per outstanding item, rendered only when there is at least one. The documents bullet can be built today and nothing has to land first: documents are optional for submission, so the frontend can reach this page with an empty collection, and it already knows that at submit time. The identifier bullet cannot fire today and should not be built until the identifier question is settled — the frontend's submit gate requires one animal-identifier record per animal (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:88-102 sets recordCountEquals against numberOfAnimals) and readiness requires every task row to be fulfilled (src/server/app/flow/section-status.js:11-15), so a notification with animals still to identify never reaches the confirmation page at all. Design release 1 does let one through, which is why it has that bullet. Whether a partly identified animal counts as outstanding is the open question in identification--identifier-completeness; build the identifier bullet with whatever answer that finding gets.

increments.title: Frontend squeezes the address picker's five-column results table into the narrow form column, so every row wraps onto three lines; Design release 1 gives the picker the full page width
increments.detail:
All five party pickers render inside the same two-thirds column every other journey page uses, and the results table does not fit it. In the captured place-of-origin picker the table's five columns — the radio, Name, Address, Country and the View details link — are packed into the left two-thirds of the page, and every row wraps: "Astra Rosales" breaks over two lines, "43 East Hague Extension, Bern, 30055" over three, "United Kingdom" over two, and "View details" over two, on all five rows. Roughly a third of the page beside the table is empty. The width is not a decision the picker takes: the shared layout reads it from `contentColumnClass` (src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:56-57), and `kit.base` hardcodes that to the form surface, `govuk-grid-column-two-thirds` (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:20-23 and :122). The picker's controller builds its view context from `kit.base` and passes nothing that would change it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/party-picker.controller.js:43-47).

Design release 1 gives the picker the whole width of the page — its view opens on `govuk-grid-column-full` (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:27) — and it is a decision taken for this page rather than a house style, because the two other addresses pages the same release serves stay in the two-thirds column: roles-and-addresses and contact-address-for-consignment both render there. The result is that every row of the captured picker reads on one line: name, then the address lines stacked one per line because the design breaks them deliberately rather than because they wrap, then the country, then "View details" against the right-hand edge.

increments.title: A Frontend trader who spots a wrong saved address on a party picker can only read it; Design release 1 links every row to the saved record, where it can be edited or deleted before the trader is returned to the picker
increments.detail:
On a Frontend party picker each row's "View details" is a disclosure that opens in place (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:28-41), revealing the saved record as a plain list built from name, address lines, country, telephone number and email address (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:15-22). The captured place-of-origin picker carries five of them, and the first opens to seven lines for Astra Rosales ending "01632 960000" and "astra-rosales@example.com". The row offers nothing else: no Edit, no Delete, no link out. So a trader who sees that a saved consignor has moved, that a postcode is wrong, or that the same farm is in the book twice, has no way to correct or remove it anywhere in this service, and the only thing they can do is pick the wrong record or abandon the section. Searching the rendered DOM of all 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "edit address", "change this address", "edit this address" and "delete address" returns nothing. This is deliberate in the code: the address-book service exposes only search, all and party, and says "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The transporter list is the same shape, its rows leading nowhere either.

In Design release 1 the same "View details" is a link out of the row to the saved address's own page, carrying the page the trader came from in a return parameter, so a row on the place-of-origin picker points at /address-book/<id>?return=%2Fplace-of-origin (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:152, with the href built at app/routes.js:3562). That page is dr1-address-book-view: the record's name as the heading, a summary list of eight facts, and then an "Edit" button beside a red "Delete" button. Edit opens dr1-address-book-edit, headed "Edit address and contact details", with all nine address and contact fields prefilled and already open, the address search suppressed, and "Save changes" beside "Cancel"; the return parameter is carried into the form action, so saving or cancelling puts the trader back on the picker they left rather than stranding them in the address book, and the delete honours the same parameter. Design release 1's transporter list links its rows to the same record page. So in Design release 1 a wrong saved address is fixed where it is noticed, and the notification is never abandoned.

Give every picker row a route to the saved record and a way back to the page the trader left. This is the maintenance half of the route the add finding covers, and it turns on the same choice of destination: either an address record page inside this frontend, which means giving its address-book service the update and delete it deliberately does not have (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19), or a link into the Import Notification Service front door's existing address-book record and edit pages, which needs a return URL so the trader comes back to the picker. The address-book API already serves update and delete, so nothing has to land first either way and the band is frontend-work. Raise it separately from the add route because it is a different control, a different user need -- correcting or removing a record rather than creating one -- and because it was until now carried by nobody: the addresses slice recorded both "View details" behaviours and passed the question to address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, and the transport slice left Design release 1's transporter "View details" link out for the same reason, but neither that finding nor the add-route finding asks for the route. Whether the in-place disclosure survives alongside the link is a design call for whoever does the work; Design release 1 shows only the link. Most of what the disclosure shows is already in the row — the name, the address lines and the country that the Name, Address and Country columns carry — so those repeated lines should come out of it when the link lands. The two runs disagree about the band: run C banded this frontend-work because the address-book API already serves update and delete, where run A banded it needs-backend because this service's own address-book client has neither. What turns on the answer is only where the record page lives — built here against the API that already exists, or linked into the Import Notification Service front door's — so the band taken here is frontend-work. The named control, "View details", occurs five times on the Frontend picker and nine times on the Design release 1 one, so both cards will be refused a crop and fall back to the whole page with the reason printed. That is the right picture here: the finding is about what a row leads to, not about one row.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any control on a Frontend party picker, transporter list or contact-address page that leads to changing or removing a saved address-book record.

increments.title: DR1's address picker puts the whole book on one page and narrows it as the trader types; the frontend shows five records at a time behind a Search button and pages through the rest.
increments.detail:
The picker shows five records at a time — `PAGE_SIZE = 5` (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:10), sliced server-side — with a govukPagination block beneath the table (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:64-66) and a secondary Search button that re-posts the whole form (:86-91). fe-address-picker-place-of-origin reads "Showing 5 of 13 addresses" over five rows, then "1 2 3 Next". Because the chosen record can be on a page the trader is not looking at, the picker has to restate it in an inset above the table, "Selected address: …" (:93-95) — a control that exists only to work around the paging. The page carries no client JavaScript by design (:7-11).

DR1 renders every address for the role in one table with no pagination anywhere on the page, and heads it "Select an address" with a live count, "Showing 9 out of 9 results" (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:93-97). The search control is a `type="search"` input with a magnifier button that does not submit (:70-90); typing in it hides non-matching rows and rewrites the count as the trader types. The captured filtered state shows "Romania" typed into it and the count reading "Showing 3 out of 9 results", with the page never reloaded: each row carries the text it is matched against and is hidden or shown on every keystroke (app/assets/javascripts/consignment-address-search.js:66-92). dr1-consignment-address-select shows all nine records at once, so a chosen radio is always visible next to Save and continue.

Show the whole role list on one page: drop PAGE_SIZE and the pagination block, put the count line above the table, and let search narrow the rendered list rather than fetch a new page. The frontend's stated no-JS baseline is the constraint DR1 does not have — DR1's magnifier button is `type="button"` and a no-JS Enter discards the query, so copying it verbatim would lose a working search for a trader without JavaScript. The portable half is one page, no pagination, count above the table, with the existing server-side search kept as the no-JS fallback and a filter layered on top. The "Selected address:" inset can go once the chosen row is always on screen. This assumes an organisation's book stays small enough for one page; if it will not, the finding is about the count line and the search behaviour rather than about removing pagination.

FALSIFIED BY: Pagination appearing in DR1's consignment-address-select template, or an address book large enough that one page is not viable.

increments.title: DR1 asks for a CPH number on every consignment except horses and the 01061900 group; the frontend asks only when the consignment contains cattle.
increments.detail:
The CPH row appears on the addresses hub, and the CPH page is reachable, only when a commodity line matches a whitelist of one entry: `CPH_COMMODITIES = ['Cow']` (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:119, applied by src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/controller.js:27-30 and src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:50-52). Everything else in the catalogue — horses, cats, dogs and fish — is never asked for a CPH number. The rule is an allow-list, so every commodity added to the catalogue from now on defaults to not being asked.

DR1 works the opposite way round: the CPH section is in the default set of address sections, and a commodity code has to be listed explicitly to escape it (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:148-160). Two live-animal codes escape — 0101, horses, and 01061900, the cat/dog/ferret group, which gets a permanent-address section instead (:101,124). Cattle and pigs are listed explicitly with CPH included (:108,116), and every other live-animal code in DR1's catalogue, from sheep and goats through poultry to ornamental fish, falls to the default and is asked for one. Two germinal-product codes, 05111000 and 05119985, are also listed without CPH (:132,139), but germinal products are outside this comparison, so they neither add to nor subtract from the rule for live animals.

Invert the rule: ask for a CPH number unless the consignment's commodity is one that is exempt, and make the exempt list horses and the 01061900 group rather than making cattle the only inclusion. Within today's five-entry catalogue this changes one commodity, fish, which DR1 asks and the frontend does not; the reason to do it anyway is that the allow-list makes every future commodity silently exempt, which is the wrong default for a question DR1 treats as the norm. Whether each newly-included commodity really needs a CPH number is a question for the catalogue work rather than for this rule.

FALSIFIED BY: A live-animal commodity code in DR1's catalogue, outside 0101 and 01061900, that is not asked for a CPH number, which would mean the default set is incidental rather than the rule.

increments.title: The frontend lets a user delete a notification and cancel an amendment from the dashboard; DR1 has neither journey, and whether they are in scope for DR1 parity is unsettled.
increments.detail:
Every card on the dashboard offers a Delete link, and a card being amended also offers Cancel amendment (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-67). Delete leads to a confirmation page headed "Delete this notification?" saying "This cannot be undone." with a red "Yes, delete notification" and "No, return to dashboard"; it is reached both from the Delete action on a dashboard card and from the Delete button at the top of a submitted notification's read-only review page. Cancel amendment leads to "Cancel this amendment?" saying the changes since amending started will be discarded and the submitted version restored, offering "Yes, cancel amendment" against "No, return to notification". Submitted cards also offer Amend, which is where the amendment being cancelled comes from.

A DR1 user has neither. The card offers Copy as new and View and nothing else (app/views/dashboard.html:257-262), and the two journeys the frontend has are unreachable: the delete page redirects to the dashboard unless the session carries the design-release-2 flag (app/routes.js:5607-5613), and cancel-amend does the same (app/routes.js:9652-9655). The delete guard is a two-part test rather than a single flag — it redirects unless the session carries the flag and the request carries a submitted or reference query parameter — and the amend entry point is gated identically (app/routes.js:9618-9620), so neither journey has a way in. Neither page has a root view either: there is no delete-notification.html and no cancel-amend.html at the root of app/views, only copies under design-release-2/ and design-release-2.1/, which are other releases' documents. There is no DR1 page to compare either frontend page against, which is why the corpus pairs neither of them.

This is the one question in this slice that needs a person rather than more evidence. Two readings are both consistent with what is on the page. Either delete and amend are design-release-2 features that shipped early in the frontend, in which case they are out of scope here and this comparison should record no finding about the pages themselves; or they are capabilities DR1 assumed without drawing, in which case DR1 is silent rather than opposed and the frontend pages need reviewing against DR2 designs, not this one. What settles it is a statement from the designer on whether delete and amend were in the DR1 scope: if they were, DR1's dashboard card is missing a Delete action and the absence is a prototype gap; if they were not, both frontend journeys are ahead of the signed-off design and belong to the next comparison. Until then, treat the two frontend pages as unassessed rather than as defects, and raise nothing about their copy, their button pattern or their confirmation wording. The frontend states are recorded so a person can look at them: fe-delete-notification, fe-cancel-amend, and fe-dashboard-deleted for what the dashboard shows afterwards.

increments.title: The hub hides the animal and package totals until a commodity has been added, where Design release 1 shows them from the start reading zero
increments.detail:
On a notification with no commodities the hub goes straight from the "Overview" heading to the first task section. There is no "Your commodities" heading and no summary of what the notification contains — the words appear in no captured frontend screen in this corpus. The frontend does build the same two summary panels, headed "Your commodities" with the labels "Animals" and "Packages/boxes" and the same captions (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:3-9, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/template.njk:8-26), but the whole block is behind a truthiness test and the view model returns null while the commodity collection is empty (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:142-151), so a user only ever meets it once they have added a commodity line.

Design release 1 shows "Your commodities" directly under the page heading on every visit to the hub, with two grey panels reading "0 Animals — Total number of animals in this consignment" and "0 Packages/boxes — Total number of packages in this consignment" before anything has been entered, and the same panels reading the real totals once commodities exist (app/views/notification-hub.html:26-50). The summary is the first thing on the page and it is never absent.

Render the commodity summary on every visit to the hub, showing zero for both totals when the notification holds no commodity lines, instead of suppressing the block. The change is the null return at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:142-151 and the guard around the block at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/template.njk:8. One layout consequence travels with it and is worth stating rather than raising twice: both sides lay the two panels out as a pair of half-width columns, but Design release 1 gives the hub the full grid width (app/views/notification-hub.html:21) while the frontend confines it to a two-thirds column, so the panels arrive narrower than the design draws them.

increments.title: The hub lists an animal identification task on a notification with no commodities, where Design release 1 adds that task only once a commodity needs identifiers
increments.detail:
"Animal identification details" is on the hub from the moment the notification is created, before any commodity has been chosen and therefore before it is known whether any animal needs an identifier at all. It shows on both captured hub states, locked with the status "Cannot start yet". The frontend does know how to leave a row out — its exit-details and transit-countries rows are marked conditional and are absent from both captures (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-47, with the hiding at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93-118) — but the identification row is not marked that way (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45), so it always appears.

Design release 1's hub has no identification task on a notification with nothing chosen: its "2. Description of the goods" section holds two rows, "Commodity details" and "Additional details". "Identification details" is inserted between them only when the commodities chosen require animal identifiers (app/routes.js:5778-5782), which is what dr1-notification-hub-partly-complete shows. So the task appears when it becomes relevant and is invisible until then.

Make the identification row conditional on the notification actually needing animal identifiers, so it is absent from the hub rather than present and locked while no commodity has been chosen. The hub already knows how to drop a row — src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:93 hides a row that is marked conditional once its status is not-applicable — but marking the identification entry conditional at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45 is not on its own enough, and the work has to allow for that. The row's status is rolled up over the commodityLines collection (:44), and commodityLines is a structural group that is in scope from the moment the notification exists (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/lines.js:18-32), so the roll-up never reaches not-applicable and the row would still be drawn. Either the row needs its own applicability test — do any chosen commodities require identifiers, which is the question Design release 1 asks at app/routes.js:5778 — or the identification obligations need a scope condition that makes the roll-up not-applicable with no commodity lines. This is a different change from unlocking the rows (inc-032): unlocking makes a shown row usable, this decides whether the row is shown at all.
