increments.title: The frontend locks all but one hub task behind the answers before it, while Design release 1 lets a user start any task on the notification in any order
increments.detail:
On a brand new notification the hub lists eleven tasks and exactly one of them can be opened. "Where is this consignment coming from?" is a link tagged "Not yet started"; the other ten rows are plain text with the grey status "Cannot start yet" and carry no link at all, so the hub offers no way into them. Answering the origin questions unlocks precisely one more row — on fe-hub-part-answered "What are you importing?" has become a link and every row below it still reads "Cannot start yet", including "Arrival details", "Upload documents" and "Contact address", none of which depends on the origin answers. Nine of the eleven rows on that page, from the reason for import through to check and submit, are plain black text with no way in, and the only two a user can open are the one they have already answered and the commodity picker itself. The hub decides this per row: src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:120-122 renders an open row or a blocked one according to whether the first page in the row passes its gate, and the gate is that page's prerequisites at src/server/app/flow/gates.js:23-32. Those prerequisites chain on two answers — country of origin and the commodity selection, the pair enforced at continue in src/server/app/bridge/obligation-source.js:30-33 — and every page that sits after them in the journey order demands them (src/server/app/flow/prerequisites.js:13-27), which is why one unanswered question closes most of the page. A conditional row whose questions are all out of scope behaves differently again: it is dropped from the list entirely rather than blocked (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:116-118), so "Exit details" is absent from such a hub rather than shown shut.

Every task on the hub is a link from the moment the notification is created, and every one carries the same status, "To do". A user can open "Upload documents", "Roles and addresses" or "Contact address for this consignment" before saying anything about the consignment, and can come back to "Main reason for import" afterwards. Design release 1 renders each row as an unconditional link (app/views/notification-hub.html:60-73) and offers no locked state and no "cannot start" wording anywhere on the page.

Drop the row gating on the hub so every task row renders as a link with a real status from the moment the notification exists, and retire the "Cannot start yet" status the hub uses for a blocked row. The gate to remove is the one the hub itself consults: rowGatePasses tests the row's first page against the per-page prerequisites at src/server/app/flow/gates.js:23-32 (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25), and the hub renders an open or a blocked row on that answer. The change does not stop at the hub, but the work is smaller than it looks in one respect and larger in another. Smaller, because nothing has to be unblocked at the route: no request handler consults those prerequisites, the only pre-handler guard being the deep-link entry guard at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js:45-57, so the pages already admit a direct visit. Larger, because that is exactly why they have never had to cope: each page behind an unlocked row has to render and save sensibly when the pages that currently precede it have not been answered. Where a page genuinely cannot be answered until something else is known — the animal identifiers need a commodity — Design release 1's answer is to leave the row out of the list until it applies, not to show it locked; that is its own finding, inc-035, on the identification row being shown before it applies.

increments.title: The hub divides a notification into different sections from Design release 1, and names five of its six section headings differently
increments.detail:
The hub's task list runs under six numbered headings: "1. About the consignment", "2. Commodity details", "3. Movement", "4. Addresses", "5. Documents", "6. Check and submit". Addresses and the consignment contact share one section; documents come fifth; and the last section exists only to hold the check-and-submit row. The headings and the rows under them are fixed in the hub's own view model at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:33-49, with the wording at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:18-25.

Design release 1 runs the same work under six different headings in a different order: "1. About the consignment", "2. Description of the goods", "3. Transport and arrival", "4. Documents", "5. Consignment parties", "6. Contact address". Only the first heading matches the frontend word for word. Documents move up to fourth; the consignment parties and the contact address are two sections rather than one; and there is no section for checking and submitting, because Design release 1 puts that on a button under the list. The whole list also sits under a heading of its own, "Notification tasklist", which the frontend does not show. Design release 1 states the sections at app/routes.js:5749-5841.

Rename and regroup the hub's six sections to match Design release 1: keep "1. About the consignment"; rename "2. Commodity details" to "2. Description of the goods"; rename "3. Movement" to "3. Transport and arrival"; promote documents to "4. Documents"; split the current "4. Addresses" into "5. Consignment parties" holding the roles-and-addresses row and "6. Contact address" holding the contact row; and delete the "6. Check and submit" section, whose row is replaced by a button (see inc-036). The first section changes too, though not by renaming: the "Exit details" row leaves it when the exit questions fold into the reason for import as conditional reveals, so section 1 loses a row while sections 2 to 6 are being renamed and resplit (see inc-069). Add the "Notification tasklist" heading above the sections. The group list at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:33-49 and the copy at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:18-25 are the two places the change lands. Which rows sit in which section is settled by this finding; what the rows are called is inc-040. This finding names no control on purpose: it is about the shape of the whole task list, so the full-page shot of each side is the evidence, and cropping to any one heading would hide the regrouping that is the point.

increments.title: DR1 tags a hub task either Complete or To do and has no third state; the frontend uses Completed, In progress, Not yet started and Optional.
increments.detail:
The frontend tags each task with one of four words or phrases (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js:11-17): 'Completed' in green, 'In progress' in light blue, 'Not yet started' in blue, and 'Optional' rendered as plain grey text with no tag around it at all. The captured hub shows all four: 'Where is this consignment coming from?' is Completed, 'What are you importing?' is In progress, most rows are Not yet started, and 'Uploaded documents' is Optional.

DR1 has exactly two statuses and every task carries one of them: 'Complete' in green or 'To do' in blue (app/routes.js:5735-5736). Every row in the captured DR1 hub, documents included, reads 'To do'. A DR1 user is never told a task is part-done, and is never told on the hub that a task is optional.

Reduce the hub's status vocabulary to DR1's two: 'Complete' where the task is finished and 'To do' everywhere else. That retires the part-done state, which DR1 does not distinguish, and the 'Optional' text on the documents row, which in DR1 is just another 'To do'. Only the words move: the frontend already maps its unstarted state to govuk-tag--blue and its finished one to govuk-tag--green (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:51-68), and DR1's 'To do' and 'Complete' carry the same two classes, so the tags themselves stay as they are. DR1 has no counterpart at all for the part-done or the optional state, so if either is to survive in some form that is a decision taken against the design rather than one the design settles. This is the wording and the set of states on the tag only — whether documents are actually optional to submit is a separate question and belongs to the documents slice, and the blocked-row presentation that carries the fifth phrase 'Cannot start yet' is its own finding, inc-032.

increments.title: A user importing horses temporarily cannot get back to their port of exit and exit date from the hub — the Exit details row is shown but has no link, even though both questions are compulsory.
increments.detail:
A user who has chosen temporary admission of horses, answered port of exit and saved it, and then returned to the hub, finds the 'Exit details' row sitting there as plain black text with nothing to click and the words 'Cannot start yet' beside it. The row is not hidden and not empty — it is the entry to two questions this reason makes compulsory, one of which the user has already answered. The picture is fe-hub-exit-details-blocked and the rendered row is a `<li class="govuk-task-list__item">` carrying no `<a>` at all, where every other startable row on the same page carries `govuk-task-list__item--with-link` and a link. The row stands for three pages in order — destination country, port of exit, exit date (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39) — and whether it is a link is decided by the first of those alone: `rowGatePasses` tests `row.pages[0]` (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25). Under this reason destination country is out of scope while port of exit and exit date are both in scope and mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:64-113), so the first page fails its gate and the whole row is shut. The status is misleading as well as the link: `blockedRowItem` throws the row's real status away and substitutes 'Cannot start yet' whatever it was (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:95,122), so a row that is genuinely in progress tells the user they cannot begin work they have already partly done. The user can still reach the two questions going forwards, because `nextInSection` walks past the out-of-scope page to the next one that passes (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:27-37), so they can complete the notification — but once they have left those pages they cannot get back to change an answer. Two lines above the faulty gate, `rowEntry` already does the right thing: it picks the first page whose gate passes (:20-23).

The question does not arise in DR1, because DR1 has no exit-details task. Port of exit and exit date are asked inline on the reason-for-import page as a conditional reveal under the temporary-admission answer, and they count towards that page's own 'Main reason for import' task (app/routes.js:1361-1364). A DR1 user returns to them by opening 'Main reason for import' again, which is always a link.

Make `rowGatePasses` agree with `rowEntry` — a row is enterable when any of its pages passes its gate, not only the first. That is a one-line change in src/server/app/flow/navigation.js and it restores the return route for the temporary-admission case. It is worth doing on its own even though the larger change of folding these questions into the reason-for-import task would remove the row altogether, because that change is bigger and this defect is live today.

FALSIFIED BY: A hub rendered with reason for import set to temporary admission of horses that shows the 'Exit details' row as a working link.

finding.correction:
The defect is real and every step of it was re-traced at frontend 76a864ba. rowGatePasses is one line and tests row.pages[0] only (src/server/app/flow/navigation.js:25); the Exit details row's pages are destination country, port of exit, exit date in that order (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:35-39); under temporaryAdmissionHorses destinationCountry is inScope false while portOfExit and exitDate are both inScope with status mandatory (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/import-reason.js:66-115); pageGatePasses fails on an out-of-scope page (src/server/app/flow/gates.js:23-32), so the row renders blocked while its status is not NA and it is therefore not hidden. The narrow framing was checked and is the right one: the section named 'consignment' holds import reason, import purpose, destination country, port of exit, exit date and additional details in one list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/flow.js:48-58), nextInSection skips the pages that fail their gate (navigation.js:27-37), and Save and continue reaches it through nextTarget, whose hub fallback only fires when the user pressed the return-to-overview button (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:76-101). So the pages are reachable going forwards and unreachable on return, which is what the finding says. Two changes made: confidence dropped from high to medium, because the state is not in the corpus at all — fe-hub is the only frontend hub shot and it was captured with no reason for import, so the conditional row is hidden in it; and the frontend slot now says that outright rather than leaving a reader to assume the picture shows a blocked row. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: fe-hub-exit-details-blocked was shot after this finding was written, and it shows the defect rather than implying it. Confidence is back to high. The capture was driven to exactly the reason this finding names — temporary admission of horses — with port of exit selected and saved and exit date left empty, and the rendered hub holds `
  • Exit details … Cannot start yet
    • ` with no anchor anywhere inside it, against `govuk-task-list__item--with-link` on the three rows above it. The falsifier was therefore put to the one test that could fire and did not fire. One thing the capture found that the finding did not say, and the frontend slot now says: the status text is not the row's own. `blockedRowItem` (hub/controller.js:95) spreads the base row and overwrites `status` with the cannot-start constant, and buildRowItem hands every gate-failing row to it (:122), so the status the row actually earned — in progress, since one of its two in-scope questions is answered and the other is not — never reaches the page. The row does not read as 'answered but inert'. It tells the user they cannot start yet, which is the opposite of true. That makes the defect worse than a missing link: it is a missing link plus a false statement about the user's own work, and whoever fixes rowGatePasses should check that the unblocked row then shows its real status.

provenance.note: A genuine miss by C, and the most valuable single item in this area because it is a live defect rather than a parity gap. Under Temporary admission horses the Exit details row stands for three pages, of which the first (destination country) is out of scope; rowGatePasses tests only row.pages[0] (flow/navigation.js:25) where rowEntry two lines above already picks the first page that passes, so the row renders as dead text tagged 'Cannot start yet' and the user can never return to answer they have already given. C's inc-051 proposes deleting hub row gating wholesale, which would fix this incidentally, but C never observes the temporary-admission dead end, never identifies the pages[0] bug, and never notes that blockedRowItem overwrites the row's real status. Grepping C for 'rowGatePasses' returns inc-051 only, and inc-051 is about a fresh notification with ten locked rows, not this case. increments.title: Design release 1 gives a trader a saved address book they can search, filter by type, add to, view, edit and delete; Frontend has no address-book page and its journey can only read the book
increments.detail:
Frontend has no address book as a page. Its service navigation carries no items, so nothing links to a saved-addresses page, and searching the rendered DOM of all 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "address book" or "add a new address" returns nothing. A trader meets the organisation's book only inside the five consignment party pickers and the contact-address page, and there only as a read-only chooser: the pickers offer a Search input hinted "Name, address or country", a secondary Search button, a five-row results table with a radio per row and a "View details" expander, pagination, and "Save and continue" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-113), and the contact-address page offers the whole book as one radio list. Nothing anywhere adds, changes or removes a record. Frontend's address-book service exposes only search, all and party, and states the split as a design decision: "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). Frontend's records also carry no address type at all, deliberately, because the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15).

Design release 1 gives the trader an address book of their own, reached from a service-navigation item on every page, and eight captured screens describe it. dr1-address-book is the list: heading "Address book", intro "Manage your addresses for use across import notifications.", a primary "Add a new address" button, a "Filter addresses" panel holding a Search box placeholdered "Search by name, address or country" and a "Type" select offering Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and Branch Address, a result count ("Showing 1-8 of 58"), a Name / Type / Address / Country table with a "View" link per row, and pagination (app/views/address-book.html:34-45). dr1-address-book-add is the type chooser: "What is the new address for?", one addressType radio group over those same seven types and a Continue button. Each type carries a hint that defines it, and the hints are as much of the requirement as the labels are, so they are quoted here in full — Place of Origin, "The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain"; Consignor, "This is the sender of the consignment."; Consignee, "This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported."; Importer, "This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed."; Place of Destination, "This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address."; Transporter, "This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment."; then a divider, and Branch Address, "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." The labels, the hints and the divider are all defined together at app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38 and rendered as govuk-radios__hint at app/views/address-book-add.html:77-80. dr1-address-book-lookup is the add form: "Add address details", a "Search for an address" type-ahead writing a hidden addressBookLookupAddressId, an "Enter address manually" toggle, "Save and continue" and "Cancel and return to address book". dr1-address-book-lookup-results is that page with the type-ahead panel open over candidate addresses. dr1-address-book-lookup-manual is that page with the manual reveal open, showing nine fields under two headings: Address (Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country) and Contact details (Email address, Phone number, hinted "For international numbers include the country code"). dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker is the same add form entered from a consignment party picker, with the type chooser skipped because the section implies the type and its answer carried in a hidden addressType. dr1-address-book-view is one saved address, headed with its own name, presented as a summary list of eight of those nine facts — County (optional) is not shown — with an "Edit" button and a red "Delete" button. dr1-address-book-edit is "Edit address and contact details": all nine fields, prefilled and already open, the search hidden, "Save changes" and "Cancel". So Design release 1's book is create, read, update and delete, and every saved address carries a type.

This is the one scope question in this comparison that a person has to settle, and it is stated here rather than decided. Two previous runs dropped these screens without photographing them; this run photographed all eight and they are enumerated above. The evidence for OUT of scope is strong, and it is not the reasoning either previous run used: the Import Notification Service front door, trade-imports-ins-frontend, already implements this address book at Design release 1's own URLs — /address-book, /address-book/add, /address-book/{id}, /address-book/{id}/edit and /address-book/{id}/delete — and its add form carries exactly the nine field labels above in Design release 1's wording, down to the phone hint; the address-book service behind it already serves create, update and delete; and this frontend's own service says writing belongs to that other service (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The evidence for IN scope is that Design release 1 puts the book behind a service-navigation item on the same service as the notification journey (app/views/layouts/main.html:16) and routes into it from inside a notification (app/routes.js:3598-3600), so to a user it is one service and not two. What settles it is one thing a person can state: whether the trade-imports-ins-frontend address book is the address book Design release 1 describes. It is not yet the same book in one respect that the person deciding should know about: Design release 1 types every saved address and offers a Type filter over seven types, while the INS front door's add form asks for no type, its list has no Type column, and the address book API's locked wire contract (OperatorResponse in trade-imports-address-book) carries no type or role field — so whichever service owns these pages, the seven address types are unbuilt everywhere. If the INS book is Design release 1's book, this finding is struck and the work left in this repo is the route out of a party picker, raised separately as address-book--no-route-to-add-an-address-from-a-picker because it stands whichever way this goes, and the address types, raised separately as addresses--pickers-offer-the-whole-address-book because they bite inside the notification journey today. If it is not, this becomes one add-page piece of work covering all eight screens above, plus a write path in Frontend's address-book service. controls is deliberately empty: the finding is that eight whole pages have no counterpart, and cropping any single control on them would show less than the page does.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a route in trade-imports-animals-frontend that renders a saved-address list, add, view, edit or delete page. Searching src/server for "address-book" returns the read-only service, its client and its callers, and no registered path beginning /address-book.

decision.note: Descoped by Sam, 2026-08-21: a separate epic folds the address book in. This finding asked the one scope question the run could not settle — whether the trade-imports-ins-frontend address book is the book Design release 1 describes — and the answer is that it is, and it belongs to that epic rather than to this frontend. The eight DR1 address-book screens are struck from this backlog. The finding predicted this outcome and named what survives it: the route out of a party picker (inc-053, inc-054) and the seven address types, which bite inside the notification journey whichever service owns the book.

finding.correction: Two changes. (1) The author wrote that dr1-address-book-view presents "those same nine facts". It presents eight: dr1-address-book-view.html has exactly eight govuk-summary-list__key rows — Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address, Phone number — and County (optional) is absent, which the screenshot confirms. The prototype slot now says eight of the nine, and says "all nine" of the edit page, where all nine labels are present (dr1-address-book-edit.html carries address-book-manual-county). (2) The difference slot's settling question is unchanged, but one true fact bearing directly on it was missing and has been added: the INS front door implements Design release 1's URLs and field labels but not its type model — its add form asks no address type, its list has no Type column, and the address-book API's wire contract carries no type or role field. Everything else the author claimed was checked and stands, including the eight-screen enumeration, the INS URL set, the INS field labels, and the read-only service comment quoted verbatim. (3) NOT A CORRECTION — AN ADDITION, MADE BY THE CORPUS EDITOR BEFORE THE FIRST INGEST, RECORDED HERE SO THE CHANGE IS NOT SILENT. The prototype slot said the seven addressType radios came "each with its own hint" without quoting them, while quoting the nine manual-entry field labels verbatim beside it. Those hints are substantive domain definitions of the same class as the labels — Place of Destination defines the 48-hour accommodation rule, Importer states the default relationship to the consignee, Branch Address defines responsibility from entry until checks complete — and whoever implements these pages needs them. All seven are now quoted in the prototype slot, read from app/data/address-book-address-types.js:1-38 where the label, hint and divider are defined together, and checked against this run's own captured DOM of dr1-address-book-add, which renders all seven as govuk-radios__hint with the same text. Nothing already in the slot was altered. increments.title: Frontend refuses to let a user lower the number of animals below the identification records already entered for that species; Design release 1 accepts the lower number and shows only that many records.
increments.detail:
A user who has entered identification details for two Bos taurus and then comes back and changes the count to 1 is held on the page. The error summary and the field both read "You have 2 identifier records for Bos taurus but entered 1 animal. Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.", and the summary link sends the user to the identification card for that line rather than to the box they just typed in. Nothing is saved until they either put the number back up or go and delete records by hand (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/validation/count-drop.js:13-33).

The same change is accepted. The count is checked only for presence and for being a whole number of at least one (app/routes.js:817-848); there is no comparison against what has already been entered, and no message of that kind exists anywhere in Design release 1. The identification page then draws exactly as many animal slots as the new count asks for, so the surplus record simply stops being shown and stops counting towards completeness.

Stop refusing the submission. Follow Design release 1: accept the lower count and let the identification page show that many records. What the frontend does with the surplus record has to be decided as part of the work — Design release 1 leaves it in the session and stops rendering it, so it neither warns nor deletes — and whichever way that goes, the user is no longer stopped at the consignment-details page. Removing the rule takes the message out of the commodities copy file with it (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:38-39) and the Welsh file beside it. Nothing has to land first.

FALSIFIED BY: Design release 1 refusing a reduced count, or warning about surplus identification records. Its consignment-details handler runs four validators — animals, packages, net weight and package type — and none of them reads the saved identifiers; a fifth check, or any message naming identifier records, would prove this wrong.

decision.note: The frontend implementation is right compared to the design. Design release 1 accepts the lower count and simply stops rendering the surplus identifier record, leaving data the trader entered orphaned in the session with neither a warning nor a deletion. The frontend holds the user on the consignment-details page until they either remove the records or restore the count, which is the correct behaviour. Keep the frontend as built; the count-drop rule and its copy stay. Ruled by Sam, 2026-08-21.

increments.title: The frontend puts an example hint under Number of animals — 'For example, 1, 25 or 5000.' — that DR1 does not have.
increments.detail:
Each Number of animals input carries the hint 'For example, 1, 25 or 5000.' (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:27-30, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/consignment-details/_species-quantities.njk:11-20). On a consignment with several species the hint repeats under every line.

DR1's Number of animals input has a label and nothing else — no hint element and no aria-describedby on the input, where the packages input on the same page does carry a hint (app/views/consignment-details.html:105-114). The two sides agree on the packages hint word for word, so the difference is confined to this one field.

increments.title: A dashboard card's links change with the notification's status and a draft can only be resumed, never viewed; Design release 1 gives every card the same two links, Copy as new and View
increments.detail:
Each card's link row is built from the notification's status, so a trader meets a different set on different cards (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-67). A draft gets Resume, Copy as new and Delete; a submitted notification gets View, Amend, Copy as new and Delete; one being amended gets Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment and Delete. The captured draft cards show exactly three links — Resume, Copy as new, Delete. There is no way to look at a draft without re-entering it: Resume goes to the task list (`hubPath`) and View exists only once the notification has been submitted, when it opens Check your answers.

Design release 1 gives every card the same two links whatever its status, side by side after the reference and separated by a divider: "Copy as new" and "View" (app/views/dashboard.html:258-262, which carries no status condition of any kind). The captured dashboard shows four cards — two "Submitted", two "Submitted action required" — and all four carry that identical pair. Design release 1 offers no Resume, no Delete, no Amend and no Cancel amendment on a card, and its View is the way into a draft as much as into a submitted one: for a draft the link is built as `/review-notification?reference=…` and for a submitted one as `/review-notification?submitted=…`, so both open the review page and a trader continues a draft by following the Change links from there.

Make the card's link row fixed rather than status-driven, and offer View on every card. In src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:18-67 the three status branches collapse to one list; "View" replaces "Resume" as the label on a draft and points at Check your answers, the same target it already uses on a submitted notification, which makes the read-only view reachable for a draft for the first time. The order the design shows is Copy as new then View, which is the reverse of the frontend's current copy-then-open order for a draft. Two things are deliberately outside this finding. Delete, Amend and Cancel amendment are the frontend-only journeys already recorded as inc-026, where they are banded disputed pending an artefact that either specifies or rules them out; do not strip those links on the strength of this finding. And whether the frontend should keep a separate route back into a half-finished draft's task list is a question about the hub, not about the card — Design release 1 does not offer one, and if the answer is that it should be kept then it is a third link beside these two, not a replacement for View.

FALSIFIED BY: A status condition around the action block in Design release 1's dashboard card, or a card in the captured dr1-dashboard carrying anything other than Copy as new and View. Extracting every `app-dashboard-notification-card__action` from capture/html/prototype/dr1-dashboard.html gives eight links across four cards, alternating "Copy as new" and "View" and nothing else.

increments.title: Frontend's dashboard always has an ordering applied and no way to have none; Design release 1's sort control loads unselected, so the list starts in whatever order the service returns it
increments.detail:
There is no unsorted state anywhere in the dashboard. Every option in the select names an ordering, and one of them is always in force: the controller parses the sort query parameter and falls back to a default when it is absent or unrecognised (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:53, through parseNotificationSort at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/notification-helper.js:58-60), and the picture of fe-dashboard-populated shows "Arrival (newest to oldest)" already selected on a page the trader has not touched. The default is carried all the way to the notification list read, which defaults the parameter again and interpolates it unconditionally into the request (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26 and :34). So a trader cannot see the list in the order the service returns it, and the page never has to answer the question of what to show when nothing has been chosen.

Design release 1's select loads on "Select one", an unselected placeholder ahead of its three orderings (app/data/dashboard-notifications.js:147-152), and the captured DOM of dr1-dashboard shows it selected. So the design's starting state is a list with no ordering named. The design does not say what that order should be, and it cannot be read off the prototype: getDashboardViewModel reads the sort parameter, hands it to buildDashboardSortItems so the right option shows as selected and to the pagination hrefs, and never orders the notification list by it (app/routes.js:7138-7255), so the prototype's list is in fixture order whatever the select says.

Give the dashboard a state in which no ordering has been chosen, and decide what the list query does in it. Two things have to happen in Frontend. The sort control needs an unselected entry that is not an ordering, which means the default at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/notification-helper.js:58-65 stops being applied when the trader has chosen nothing rather than being applied silently. Then the notification list read has to be able to ask for a page without an ordering: src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26 defaults sort to arrivalDate,desc and :34 puts it in the query string on every call, so the parameter has to become optional there and the stub at src/server/app/services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:18 has to match. The band is frontend-work because both edits are Frontend's and the frontend can build and run this against its own stub today — but confirm with the notifications API's owners what order it returns when no sort parameter is sent before this ships, because that order is what a trader will actually see and neither this design nor the prototype specifies it. Adding the "Select one" label to the options list is part of the copy change raised as inc-023; this finding is what the label has to mean.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a request from Frontend's dashboard for a page of notifications that carries no sort parameter, or an option in Frontend's sort select that is not an ordering. src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26 and :34 default the parameter and always send it, and the four options at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:27-36 are all orderings.

decision.note: Carried from run C inc-098, rejected by Sam on 2026-08-21, upgrading that day's earlier deferral. Keep the frontend's always-sorted dashboard; Design release 1's unselected sort control is not to be adopted. The dashboard is temporary, so no sort work is wanted.

increments.title: DR1's dashboard tells a user which submitted notifications still need something from them with a "Submitted action required" status; the frontend can only ever say Draft, Submitted, Amending or Deleted.
increments.detail:
The status tag on a card comes from a fixed map of four journey states: Draft (blue), Submitted (green), Amending (yellow) and Deleted (grey) (src/server/app/shared/kit.js:34-51). Once a notification is submitted it reads Submitted and stays that way, so a user scanning the list cannot tell a notification that is progressing from one that is waiting on them.

Two of the four cards on DR1's dashboard carry an orange "Submitted action required" tag beside the green "Submitted" of the others (app/views/dashboard.html:269-278, values from app/data/dashboard-notifications.js:7). DR1's status filter names a wider set again — Draft, Submitted, In progress, Approved, Action required, Rejected and Complete — so the dashboard is meant to report where a notification has got to after submission, not just that it was sent.

The dashboard needs to show a post-submission status that distinguishes a notification needing the user's attention from one that does not. The frontend cannot produce one today: the status on a row is the journey's own lifecycle state and there is no field on the record that carries a decision or an outstanding requirement back from the authorities. So the record contract needs a status the authorities can set, and the list read has to return it, before the tag can be added and the status filter built on top of it. Agree the full set of values at the same time — DR1 states seven in the filter but only demonstrates three on cards, so the list has to be settled against what the service really reports rather than copied from the prototype fixture.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any status a frontend notification card can show, other than Draft, Submitted, Amending and Deleted.

increments.title: The frontend's dashboard lists a draft so the user can resume it; DR1's dashboard cannot show a draft at all, while its own status filter offers Draft as something to filter by.
increments.detail:
The dashboard is where a user goes back to unfinished work. A draft appears in the list with a blue Draft tag and a Resume link that takes the user back to the notification's task list (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/view-model/row/actions.js:43-52). On the captured page the only notification in the list is a draft, so the dashboard is doing nothing else at that moment.

A DR1 user never sees a draft on the dashboard. The list the root view renders (app/views/dashboard.html:253-254) is filtered before it arrives: the dashboard always uses an in-progress view of the notifications, and that view drops every record marked as a draft and every record marked as submission-complete. The DR1 fixture holds eight notifications, two of them drafts and two of them completed, and only the remaining four ever appear — which is why the page reads "Show 1-4 of 4 results". Nothing in the root design offers a way to see the other four: the root view renders no tabs and no link anywhere carries a tab, and the tab links the shared code builds all point at the design release 2.1 dashboard rather than at this one. At the same time DR1's own status filter offers Draft as one of the seven statuses a user may filter the list to (app/views/dashboard.html:153), which is a status the list it filters can never contain.

This one needs a person, because DR1 states two things that cannot both be true. Either the dashboard is deliberately a list of live consignments and drafts belong somewhere else, in which case the design owes an answer to where a user resumes unfinished work and the Draft option should come off the status filter; or the dashboard is meant to list drafts like the frontend does and the exclusion is an accident. The accident reading is the more likely one on the evidence: the filtering, the tab names and the tab links are all furniture belonging to the later design release, shared by both dashboards through one view model, and the root design uses none of it except the side effect. What settles it is a designer saying whether a draft is meant to appear on the DR1 dashboard. If it is, no frontend work follows and the note is against the prototype. If it is not, the frontend's dashboard needs a stated home for drafts before anything is removed from it, because resuming a draft is the only way back into an unfinished notification today.

FALSIFIED BY: Seeing a notification with a Draft tag in the list on DR1's dashboard at its root mount, without adding a query parameter the design never links to.

Nothing in the root design offers a way to see the other four: the root view renders no tabs and no link anywhere carries a tab, and the tab links the shared code builds all point at the design release 2.1 dashboard rather than at this one. At the same time DR1's own status filter offers Draft as one of the seven statuses a user may filter the list to (app/views/dashboard.html:153), which is a status the list it filters can never contain.
finding.difference: This one needs a person, because DR1 states two things that cannot both be true. Either the dashboard is deliberately a list of live consignments and drafts belong somewhere else, in which case the design owes an answer to where a user resumes unfinished work and the Draft option should come off the status filter; or the dashboard is meant to list drafts like the frontend does and the exclusion is an accident. The accident reading is the more likely one on the evidence: the filtering, the tab names and the tab links are all furniture belonging to the later design release, shared by both dashboards through one view model, and the root design uses none of it except the side effect. What settles it is a designer saying whether a draft is meant to appear on the DR1 dashboard. If it is, no frontend work follows and the note is against the prototype. If it is not, the frontend's dashboard needs a stated home for drafts before anything is removed from it, because resuming a draft is the only way back into an unfinished notification today.
finding.correction: Written by the verifier, not the author. The author found the mechanism, judged it absurd against a frontend whose dashboard exists so a user can resume a draft, and left it out of the corpus as a paragraph in a report. I verified the mechanism and disagree with leaving it out. It holds, and it is broader than described: the same filter hides completed notifications as well as drafts, so four of DR1's eight fixture records are unreachable, not two. It is also sharper than described, because DR1 contradicts itself here rather than merely being odd — a design cannot both offer "filter the list to Draft" and render a list that can never hold one. That contradiction is what the disputed band exists for, and a known inconsistency in a signed-off design is exactly the thing that gets rediscovered expensively once someone builds against it. Checked by reading the shared dashboard view model, confirming the root view references none of the tab model, confirming no view links to a tab, counting the fixture records by their variant, and counting the four cards in capture/html/prototype/dr1-dashboard.html against the eight in the fixture. One honest caveat: the tab value is read from the query string, so a hand-typed address at the root mount would render the drafts. The design never links to it, so no user reaches it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Seeing a notification with a Draft tag in the list on DR1's dashboard at its root mount, without adding a query parameter the design never links to.

relatedTo.why: the Draft option in DR1's status filter is one half of the contradiction this finding names, so whoever settles the option set settles this too
the count DR1 prints is the count after the hidden filter, so it reads 4 of 4 rather than 4 of 8

provenance.note: Nothing in C's backlog touches this — no mention of the in-progress view, of the eight-record fixture, or of the four records that never render. A genuine miss, and it undercuts one of C's own claims: C inc-094 asserts DR1's View "is the way into a draft as much as into a submitted one", reasoning from a conditional href in the card template that DR1's own list can never exercise, because the list is filtered to drop drafts before it arrives. A found the contradiction DR1 contains (a Draft option on a status filter over a list that can never hold one) and correctly banded it disputed pending a designer. This is the single biggest thing run C does not tell you.

increments.title: Five journey pages end with a save-and-return button and a cancel link that Design release 1 does not show there, where the design ends the page with one button
increments.detail:
Every journey page that renders the shared save-actions macro gets all three of its controls, because the macro takes no argument that would drop one (src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13): a primary "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to hub" and a "Cancel and return to hub" link. The two return controls appear together on 41 of the 67 captured frontend screens, and on every screen where either appears the other does too. So a user meets the same three-way choice at the foot of the origin page, the CPH number page, the contact-address page, the transporter-type page and the private-transporter page.

Design release 1 shows the three-control pattern on 29 of its 60 captured screens and ends the other journey pages with a single button. On five pages that pair with frontend pages carrying the full set it shows one control and no way to leave: origin-of-the-import, cph-number and transporter-add-private end with "Save and continue" alone — the origin page's whole form-actions block is one button at app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:167-175 — and contact-address-for-consignment and transporter-add end with a button reading just "Continue". The private-transporter page is the one exception with a second control, and it is a third destination rather than the overview — a "Cancel and return to dashboard" link.

Stop rendering the secondary button and the cancel link on the five pages the design ends with one button, and leave the pattern intact on the pages that keep it. The macro at src/server/app/shared/save-actions.njk:3-13 renders all three unconditionally, so it needs a way to ask for the primary alone — a flag on the macro, read by the five feature templates — rather than five copies of a shortened button group. Two of the five also differ in the primary label, "Continue" against "Save and continue", and one carries a cancel link to the dashboard rather than the overview; those are copy on individual pages and belong with whoever picks up this change, not with the shared macro. Design release 1 states no rule for which pages carry the full pattern, so the design's own list is the specification: the five named here lose it and the rest keep it.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding "Save and return to overview" or "Cancel and return to overview" in the captured DOM of dr1-origin-of-the-import, dr1-cph-number, dr1-contact-address-for-consignment, dr1-transporter-add or dr1-transporter-add-private.

finding.verification: Written and checked by the verifier, so a reader knows both were the same pass. Ran the falsifier: neither string occurs in any of those five prototype files. Listed both sides exhaustively — "Save and return to hub" is in 41 of the 67 frontend files and "Cancel and return to hub" in the same 41; "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview" are each in 29 of the 60 prototype files — then walked every entry in pairs.cjs to find the pairs where the two sets disagree, which are the five named. Extracted the button text on each: fe-origin, fe-cph-number, fe-contact, fe-transporter-type and fe-transporter-private each carry all three, dr1-origin-of-the-import, dr1-cph-number and dr1-transporter-add-private carry "Save and continue", the last also carrying "Cancel and return to dashboard", and dr1-contact-address-for-consignment and dr1-transporter-add carry a submit button whose text is "Continue". Opened evidence/frontend@76a864ba/page/fe-origin.png and evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-origin-of-the-import.png, which show the difference plainly: three controls against one.

C also spots what A does not — DR1's private-transporter page carries a cancel link to a THIRD destination, the dashboard, not the overview — and identifies the shared macro at save-actions.njk:3-13 as taking no argument that could drop a control, so the fix is one flag rather than five shortened button groups. A BA should treat this as C's most substantive new item after inc-104.

decision.note: Carried from run C inc-106, rejected by Sam on 2026-08-21. Do not port Design release 1's page-by-page button pattern; both sides are internally inconsistent and copying the design's page list would import that inconsistency. Superseded by a new finding that makes the buttons consistent everywhere as a first pass.

increments.title: The frontend puts a back link on the notification overview; in DR1 the overview is the top of the notification and has none.
increments.detail:
The overview page — the task list for a notification — carries a "Back" link pointing at the dashboard (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:167). It is the only page in the service that renders no breadcrumb trail, so the back link is its sole route out, and it is labelled "Back" rather than naming where it goes.

DR1's overview page has no back link — its `beforeContent` block at app/views/notification-hub.html:9-16 renders the phase banner and nothing else, where every DR1 journey page adds a back link after it. It is the top of the notification, and the way out of it is the Dashboard item in the service navigation bar, which is on every page. Of DR1's 40 captured screens, the six without a back link are the four dashboard states, the overview and the confirmation page — every page that is a starting point rather than a step.

Stop rendering the back link on the overview page. This depends on the navigation bar carrying a Dashboard item first: the overview has no breadcrumb, so the back link is currently the only way off the page short of the browser's own, and removing it before the navigation is populated would strand the user. Sequence it after the navigation work.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding a back link rendered on DR1's notification-hub view or in its captured DOM.

finding.correction: Claim sound; one field fixed. Re-derived from the DOMs: 6 of the 40 DR1 screens render no back link and they are exactly the four dashboard states, the overview and the confirmation, as the finding says; 3 of the 33 frontend screens render none — the confirmation and the two dashboards — so the overview is the sole page where the two sides disagree, and the finding is the only thing that difference can be. Both frontend citations are exact: `backLink: dashboardPath()` is at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/hub/controller.js:167, inside the cited :160-170. both remove a route out of a page that the populated navigation bar replaces

provenance.note: A genuine C miss, and I verified it against C's OWN evidence: C's fe-hub capture (frontend@76a864ba) still shows a "Back" link above the Draft tag, so the difference is live at C's commit, not something that went away between runs. C's inc-092 walks right past it — it notes the overview is the one page that opts out of breadcrumbs, then rules back links out of scope with "The Back link stays as it is; where it points is not in question here". It asked where the back link points, never whether the page should have one. Nothing in C's 125 findings mentions it: a grep of the whole C backlog for back-link language returns only inc-054, inc-062 and inc-092, none of which is about the overview. A also gets the generalisation right — the six DR1 screens with no back link are all starting points rather than steps — and correctly sequences it behind the navigation work, because with no breadcrumb the back link is currently the overview's only route out.

increments.title: Every browser tab and bookmark in DR1 reads "Page - Import notification service - GOV.UK"; the frontend drops the GOV.UK suffix and joins with a pipe.
increments.detail:
The browser tab, the bookmark and the screen-reader announcement of every page read "Origin of the import | Import notification service" — page name, a pipe, service name, and nothing more. All 33 captured screens follow it, because it is composed once at src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:17. Nothing identifies the page as a GOV.UK service in the tab, and the pipe is not the separator the rest of GOV.UK uses. The one thing the frontend does that DR1 does not is prefix the title with "Error: " when the page is showing validation errors, which is the documented GOV.UK behaviour and should survive any change here.

DR1 titles every page "Origin of the import - Import notification service - GOV.UK" — page name, service name and GOV.UK, joined by hyphens. All 40 captured screens use it. Each view supplies only its own page name (app/views/origin-of-the-import.html:11 sets "Origin of the import") and the surrounding format is composed once for the whole prototype.

Change the title composition at src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:17 to join the page name, the service name and "GOV.UK" with hyphens, keeping the existing "Error: " prefix in front of the whole thing. Feature copy does not change — every page already supplies just its own name. Any spec that asserts on a full page title will need updating. Worth saying plainly what this rests on: unlike the phase banner and the navigation bar, this format is the Prototype Kit's default composition rather than something DR1's designers wrote, so DR1 is weak evidence on its own. It is worth doing because it is also the GOV.UK Design System's documented title convention, which the frontend's pipe form is not.

FALSIFIED BY: Finding any frontend page whose title ends in "- GOV.UK", or any DR1 page whose title uses a pipe.

finding.correction: Claim sound; one field fixed. Counts re-derived from the page models: all 33 frontend titles are "<page> | Import notification service" and all 40 DR1 titles are "<page> - Import notification service - GOV.UK", with no exception on either side. The caveat the finding volunteers is exactly right and now has a line behind it: the format is composed by the Prototype Kit at govuk-prototype-kit/layouts/govuk-branded.njk:24, `{% if pageName %}{{ pageName }} - {% endif %}{{ serviceName }} - GOV.UK`, and DR1's views supply only `pageName`, so DR1 states nothing here and the case rests on the GOV.UK Design System convention alone. It still stands as one finding rather than a nit: it is a single change to one line of the shared layout, and what it changes is what a user reads in the tab, the bookmark and the screen-reader page announcement of all 33 pages. The "Error: " prefix is confirmed present in the frontend (src/server/app/shared/copy.en.js:12, with a Welsh pair) and absent from DR1's error captures, and keeping it is right: the Design System asks for that prefix whenever an error summary is shown, so on this one point the frontend follows GOV.UK and DR1 does not. The `controls` entry was the title string written as a visible label; a page title is not an element on the page, so the crop would have found nothing. Set to an empty array, which the contract reads as a stated whole-page choice.

provenance.note: C saw this and deliberately declined it. Its inc-099 quotes DR1's full title "Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK" and then says in terms: "The separator and the absence of a GOV.UK suffix are not in question; only the page name is." So this is a scoping disagreement, not a miss — and A argues the weaker side of it honestly: it flags that unlike the phase banner and the nav bar, the hyphen-and-GOV.UK format is the Prototype Kit's default composition rather than something DR1's designers wrote, so DR1 is thin evidence on its own. A justifies raising it on the separate ground that it is the GOV.UK Design System's documented convention and the pipe is not. Worth keeping for that reason, but a BA should read it as a Design System conformance item rather than a DR1 parity gap. A also records the one thing to preserve through any change: the frontend's "Error: " title prefix, which DR1 lacks and which is correct GOV.UK behaviour.
